end-of-dennard-scaling-2004.summary: In May 2004 Intel cancelled Tejas, its next chip built for higher clock speeds, because it ran too hot; clock speeds stopped rising and computers gained cores instead. Dennard's 1974 rule had held that shrinking transistors kept power per unit area constant, so chipmakers could raise clock speeds each generation without chips running hotter; by around 2005, leakage current no longer shrank with size and chips hit a power wall. Clock speeds stalled at 4 to 6 GHz, and manufacturers turned to multicore processors to keep improving performance.

Graphene is carbon one atom thick, its atoms locked in a honeycomb pattern; on microscopic scales it is the strongest material ever measured. Geim and Novoselov shared the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for their experiments on it.

microplastics-term-2004.summary: In 2004 Richard Thompson's paper named microplastics, fragments found in sediment since the 1960s. Microplastics are plastic particles up to 5 millimetres across; they enter oceans and soils from cosmetics, clothing fibres, packaging and industrial pellets, and one 2014 estimate put 15 to 51 trillion pieces in oceans worldwide.

Membership was initially restricted to Harvard College students; Eduardo Saverin had agreed with Zuckerberg to invest $1,000 each, and Dustin Moskovitz, Andrew McCollum, and Chris Hughes joined to help manage its growth.

maori-television-launch-2004.summary: Established under Māori Television Service Act 2003, which cites Crown obligations under Treaty of Waitangi to protect te reo Māori, channel went to air on 28 March 2004 from Newmarket, Auckland. Programming mixed language learning, news, documentary and sport with a goal of revitalising a language spoken fluently by a shrinking share of Māori. A full-immersion channel Te Reo followed in 2008. Smith and Abel's 2014 paper examines its dual mandate to serve Māori and build a national audience; Abel's chapter analyses its Anzac Day coverage, which drew record ratings. It followed kōhanga reo movement and iwi radio and preceded Whakaata Māori rebrand in 2022.

Gmail moved to 4 gigabytes in October 2007 and to 15 gigabytes shared across Google services in 2013, and is now the world's largest email service, with 1.8 billion users.

medellin-metrocable-2004.summary: On 7 August 2004 Medellín's Metro company opened Metrocable Line K, a two-kilometre gondola line climbing from Acevedo metro station to Santo Domingo Savio on Comuna 1 and 2 hillsides, informal neighbourhoods built by displaced families during decades of violence. Gondolas carried up to 3,000 passengers an hour each way, cut a journey of over an hour by bus and foot to about ten minutes and were integrated into metro fares. Mayor Sergio Fajardo paired Line K with 'social urbanism': España Library Park, schools and public space at stations. Brand and Dávila's 2011 study examined travel time, safety and pride effects while cautioning that cable cars served a minority of trips. Further lines followed in 2008 and 2010, and Caracas, Rio de Janeiro, La Paz and Mexico City adopted urban cable cars.

vioxx-withdrawal-2004.summary: In September 2004 Merck withdrew the painkiller Vioxx after a trial linked it to heart attacks; tens of thousands had died. Approved in 1999 for arthritis and pain, Vioxx had earned Merck $2.5 billion in its final year on sale. Disclosures followed that Merck had withheld risk information from doctors and patients for over five years; in November 2007 it agreed to pay $4.85 billion to settle some 27,000 lawsuits.

camel-racing-robot-jockeys-2005.summary: After years of reports on trafficked boys from South Asia and Sudan riding racing camels, Qatar and United Arab Emirates ban under-age jockeys in 2005 and introduce robot riders. Swiss firm K-Team builds Qatar's first prototypes; UAE's version, made cheaper in local workshops, weighs a few kilograms, straps to saddle and carries a whip arm and speaker driven by owners following in SUVs along track, who shout at camels through walkie-talkies. UAE Federal Law 15 of 2005 sets 18 as minimum age and repatriation programmes with UNICEF return over a thousand children. Robots spread to Saudi Arabia, Oman and Kuwait, and racing camels' speeds rise with lighter loads. Case becomes a textbook example of a technical fix enabling a rights reform that pressure alone had not achieved.

mxit-mobile-chat-2005.summary: Herman Heunis's Clockspeed Mobile in Stellenbosch launched Mxit in 2005 as an instant-messaging client that ran over GPRS data on inexpensive Java feature phones. Because it used cheap GPRS data rather than SMS, teenagers adopted it in huge numbers. By 2008 it reported 7.5 million users, 6.5 million in South Africa, and by 2010 claimed 26 million registered users there. Township youth treated it as a social space as much as a messaging tool. Naspers bought a stake in 2007, and Mxit added games, music and a currency called moola before smartphone apps such as WhatsApp displaced it; it closed in 2016.

reprap-2005.summary: In 2005 Adrian Bowyer founded RepRap, a 3D printer that could print most of its own parts: desktop 3D printing. He was a mechanical engineering lecturer at the University of Bath. Its designs and software were free to download, and its first printer to copy its own parts followed in 2007.

youtube-2005.summary: In February 2005 three PayPal alumni founded YouTube; anyone could broadcast video, and Google paid $1.65 billion within 21 months. Karim had been unable to find clips of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami online. Google bought the video-sharing site for $1.65 billion on November 13, 2006. By January 2024 it had more than 2.7 billion monthly users watching over one billion hours of video every day.

y-combinator-2005.summary: In March 2005 Paul Graham started Y Combinator, funding batches of startups for a small stake, with programs in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Mountain View, California. It has since helped start more than 5,000 companies, including Airbnb, Dropbox, Stripe, Cruise, Twitch and Scale AI; over 400 are worth more than $100 million.

exenatide-glp1-2005.summary: In April 2005 the FDA approved exenatide, a diabetes drug copied from Gila monster venom; its GLP-1 class became today's weight loss drugs. Amylin developed exenatide as its synthetic version, an injected type 2 diabetes drug that mimics GLP-1, a gut hormone, raising pancreatic insulin release and curbing excess glucagon. FDA approved it in April 2005 for people whose diabetes was not well controlled on other oral medications, making it first in its class.

git-2005.summary: In 2005 Linus Torvalds began writing Git, which now tracks changes to most of the world's software. He did so after BitKeeper, proprietary software Linux's kernel had used since 2002, lost its free license for Linux. He announced Git on 6 April, and it became self-hosting a day later. By 2022 nearly 95% of developers reported Git as their primary version control system.

a380-first-flight-2005.summary: In April 2005 Airbus's A380 first flew, the largest airliner ever at 421 tonnes; airlines wanted smaller planes and it ended in 2021. Test pilots Jacques Rosay and Claude Lelaie led a crew of six on its maiden flight. Wiring problems delayed production by two years; Singapore Airlines took first delivery on 15 October 2007, and Airbus ended production in 2021 without recouping an estimated $25 billion in development costs.

malawi-input-subsidy-2005.summary: After a 2005 harvest failure left about five million Malawians needing food aid, President Bingu wa Mutharika's government defied donor advice and issued coupons for two 50 kg bags of fertiliser and 3 kg of hybrid maize seed per farming household, at about a third of market price. Some 3.4 million coupons went out in 2005-06 at a cost near US$58 million. Helped by good rains, national maize harvests rose to a record 3.44 million tonnes in 2007, Malawi exported 300,000 tonnes to Zimbabwe, and donors who had opposed subsidies began funding them. Cost, targeting and dependence on rains stayed contested.

Its time was 6 hours, 53 minutes and 8 seconds, averaging 30.7 km/h. This time five vehicles finished, with Stanley ahead of Carnegie Mellon University's Sandstorm and H1ghlander. Its $2 million prize was awarded on October 9.

cuba-energy-revolution-2006.summary: Declared by Fidel Castro for 2006 after blackouts of 2004 and 2005, Revolución Energética sent social workers door to door to exchange more than nine million incandescent bulbs for compact fluorescents and to sell, on credit, Chinese refrigerators, rice cookers, pressure cookers and fans in place of old units, while residential tariffs rose steeply above a basic block. State utility UNE installed 1,854 diesel and fuel-oil generator sets in clusters across 110 municipalities, adding on the order of 2,000 megawatts, and refurbished most of the grid; long blackouts almost vanished in 2006 to 2007. The programme cut peak demand and oil use per household, though reliance on imported fuel and Venezuelan oil remained, and grid collapses returned in the 2020s.

Distributed capacity added in 2006 differs: Lovins gives 1,820 MW for 1,854 sets, Cuban-sourced accounts say more than 3,000 MW; Käkönen et al. count 2,497 MW of distributed generation by 2014. Bulb count (nine million) is an official Cuban figure.
cuba-energy-revolution-2006.detail: Cuban figures on bulbs and generation capacity are official and not independently audited. Cuba presented its programme at climate talks as a national efficiency model. Measures included retiring hundreds of thousands of US-made 1950s refrigerators, raising tariffs steeply above 100 kilowatt-hours a month, and distributing electric pressure cookers so households cooked with electricity rather than kerosene. Cubans paid for appliances in instalments, and fuel-oil generator clusters were later connected to grid as base load, which exposed them to maintenance and fuel shortages in 2020s.

cuba-heberprot-p-2006.summary: In 2006 Cuba's regulator CECMED registered Heberprot-P, a recombinant human epidermal growth factor developed at Centro de Ingeniería Genética y Biotecnología in Havana for injection into base and edges of advanced diabetic foot ulcers. Trials led by José Fernández-Montequín reported granulation and closure in wounds that had failed standard care, with lower amputation rates; Cuba then ran a national programme reaching tens of thousands of patients through polyclinics. Heberprot-P was registered in more than twenty countries, with US trials allowed under a licence exception. It became a flagship of Cuba's state biotech sector built from CIGB's 1986 founding, alongside its meningitis B and hepatitis B vaccines.

cuba-heberprot-p-2006.detail: Heberprot-P's randomised trial and its clinical review both came from CIGB's own developers; independent randomised evidence outside Cuba remains limited, which qualifies claims of effect size. Heberprot-P is given as 75 microgram intralesional injections three times a week for up to eight weeks, usually in polyclinics or hospitals. Cuba reports more than 70,000 patients treated and amputation rates below 5 percent among treated cases. A US Treasury licence in 2015 allowed planning of trials in United States, which stalled.

induced-pluripotent-stem-cells-2006.summary: In 2006 Shinya Yamanaka showed four genes could turn an adult skin cell back into a stem cell, no embryo needed. He worked with Kazutoshi Takahashi in Kyoto. Such cells can become any cell type, so this removed any need for embryos and allowed stem cells matched to each patient. In 2012, Yamanaka and Sir John Gurdon received the Nobel Prize for discovering that mature cells can be reprogrammed to become pluripotent.

rotavirus-vaccine-2006.summary: In February 2006 the FDA approved a rotavirus vaccine; diarrhoea that killed half a million children a year began to recede. Rotavirus is the leading cause of severe diarrhea among young children. WHO now recommends rotavirus vaccine in all national immunization schedules; it estimated 215,000 rotavirus deaths among children under five in 2013, and one 2009 review estimated vaccination could prevent about 228,000 deaths a year.

walfa-savanna-burning-carbon-arnhem-land.summary: West Arnhem Land Fire Abatement project reinstated early dry-season burning by Bininj traditional owners across 28,000 square kilometres, using helicopters to drop incendiaries, reducing late-season wildfires that release methane and nitrous oxide. Under a 17-year agreement signed in 2006, ConocoPhillips paid for 100,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent abatement a year to offset emissions from its Darwin liquefied natural gas plant. Jeremy Russell-Smith's team recorded a 37.7 percent emissions cut over first seven years. An Aboriginal company, Arnhem Land Fire Abatement (Northern Territory) Limited, runs it. A national savanna burning methodology adopted in 2012 spread model across northern Australia.

hwang-woo-suk-retraction-2006.summary: Hwang Woo-suk of Seoul National University published papers in Science in 2004 and 2005 claiming human embryonic stem cell lines derived by somatic cell nuclear transfer, including eleven patient-specific lines, and became a national figure with government funding and a World Stem Cell Hub. Reports in November 2005 revealed that junior researchers had supplied eggs, and a university investigation in December found that stem cell lines did not exist and data had been fabricated. Editor-in-chief Donald Kennedy retracted both papers on 12 January 2006. Hwang was later convicted of embezzlement and bioethics violations, and journals tightened image and data checks after this case.

aws-launch-2006.summary: In 2006 Amazon began renting storage and virtual computers online by the hour, charging only for what was used instead of selling servers. Chris Pinkham, Willem van Biljon, and Christopher Brown developed EC2. By early 2023 AWS held 31% of cloud infrastructure spending, ahead of Microsoft Azure at 25% and Google Cloud at 11%.

google-translate-2006.summary: In 2006 Google Translate launched, learning from millions of UN documents, and free translation became ordinary. It used United Nations and European Parliament documents and transcripts to gather linguistic data, and often translated text into English before translating it into a target language. In November 2016 Google switched it to neural machine translation, which translates whole sentences at a time; by April 2016 it had over 500 million users.

lapindo-mud-volcano-2006.summary: On 29 May 2006 hot mud began erupting from rice fields about 150 metres from Banjar Panji-1, a gas exploration well drilled by Lapindo Brantas in Sidoarjo, East Java, two days after a magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck Yogyakarta 260 kilometres away. Flow reached up to 180,000 cubic metres a day, buried twelve villages, factories and a toll road under mud contained by levees, and displaced some 39,700 people, with damages and disaster costs above US$2.7 billion by 2015. Lusi still erupts. Richard Davies and Mark Tingay hold that drilling without casing triggered a blowout; Mazzini and others hold that earthquake reactivated a fault. Tingay's 2015 analysis of gas readings in well finds an earthquake trigger unlikely.

Hitwise counted 4.46 percent of all visits in the week ending 8 July; Yahoo answered that all its domains together still drew more. A profile with a song and a top eight was the first home page most teenagers ever made.

brazil-amazon-soy-moratorium-2006.summary: On 24 July 2006, after a Greenpeace campaign linked Amazon clearing to soy bought by Cargill, Bunge and ADM for McDonald's chicken, members of Brazilian oilseed associations ABIOVE and ANEC pledged not to purchase soybeans grown on Amazon land cleared after that date. Monitoring combined INPE deforestation maps, aerial surveys and farm registries; in 2008 the cut-off moved to that year and the pact became indefinite in 2016. Before this moratorium about 30 percent of soy expansion in Amazon biome came through deforestation; afterwards about one percent did. It became a model for supply-chain governance, though clearing shifted toward Cerrado and in 2024 to 2025 Mato Grosso legislators and antitrust regulators moved against it.

hpv-vaccine-gardasil-2006.summary: In 1991 Jian Zhou and Ian Frazer at the University of Queensland assembled shell proteins of HPV 16 into empty virus-like particles that provoke antibodies without viral DNA; Douglas Lowy and John Schiller at America's National Cancer Institute reached similar results on their own. CSL licensed Queensland's work in 1994 and sublicensed it to Merck. FUTURE II, a trial in 12,167 women across 13 countries, found 98 percent efficacy against precancerous cervical lesions caused by HPV 16 and 18. FDA approved Gardasil on 8 June 2006, and the first dose anywhere was given at Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane, on 28 August 2006. More than 600 million doses have followed; Australia expects to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem by 2035, while about 340,000 women a year still die of it, mostly in poorer countries.

iter-agreement-2006.summary: In November 2006 seven partners, China, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea, America and the European Union, signed a treaty to build ITER, a fusion reactor larger than any before, at Cadarache in southern France. Fusion joins light atomic nuclei as stars do, and ITER is meant to show it can yield net energy. Construction began in 2013; first plasma is now expected in 2033 or 2034.

hajj-crowd-dynamics-jamarat-2007.summary: On 12 January 2006 a crush at Jamarat Bridge in Mina kills at least 346 pilgrims. Saudi authorities hand security-camera footage to physicist Dirk Helbing's team, who track thousands of individuals frame by frame and find a transition from laminar flow to stop-and-go waves and then to 'crowd turbulence', in which people are pushed in all directions and fall. Their 2007 analysis gives a measurable warning signal, a pressure index from local density and velocity variance, and recommends one-way routes and timed access. Saudi planners rebuild Jamarat as a five-level structure with 12 entry and exit ramps, assign pilgrim groups time slots and install cameras feeding density monitoring.

m-pesa-2007.summary: In 2007 M-Pesa let Kenyans without bank accounts hold money on a basic mobile phone, send it to others by PIN-secured text message and pay for goods and services; most Kenyan adults used it within years. Users deposit and withdraw cash through agents, including airtime resellers and shops, paying fees to send and withdraw. M-Pesa has since expanded to Tanzania, Mozambique, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lesotho, Ghana, Egypt and Ethiopia.

cuda-2007.summary: In 2007 Nvidia let programmers run ordinary code on graphics chips, and gaming hardware became AI's engine. CUDA removed any need for graphics-programming tricks to use those chips' many small cores. It lets programmers write ordinary code that runs on Nvidia graphics chips, which contain many small processing cores built for drawing 3D scenes, and so use them for general computing, without graphics-programming skills earlier interfaces demanded. That broadened GPUs into artificial intelligence and scientific computing.

Its pilot began with 150 pupils in Villa Cardal, a village in Florida department; by late 2007 every child and teacher in that department had one. The attacks came amid a dispute with Russia over Estonia's relocation of the Bronze Soldier, a Soviet war memorial, though no concrete evidence tied Russia's government to them. Most were distributed denial of service attacks, in which many computers flood a site until it cannot answer legitimate visitors; Estonia blocked foreign traffic at times to stay online. Estonia and six other nations set up NATO's Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence in Tallinn in 2008.

jubilee-oil-ghana-2007.summary: In June 2007 Kosmos Energy's Mahogany-1 well, 60 km off Ghana's western coast, hit about 270 m of oil-bearing sands; Tullow's Hyedua-1 confirmed a single field, named Jubilee for Ghana's fiftieth independence year. Partners including Ghana National Petroleum Corporation ordered a converted tanker as floating production vessel, FPSO Kwame Nkrumah, and produced first oil on 28 November 2010, with a ceremony on 15 December, a US$3.3 billion development in about forty months. Ghana passed petroleum revenue management law in 2011 to ring-fence funds. Scholars have since debated whether oil revenues reinforced or weakened Ghanaian institutions.

Jubilee's reservoirs lie in about 1,100 m of water, and FPSO Kwame Nkrumah was built from a converted tanker in Singapore. Early production fell short of targets owing to well completion problems, and Ghana's 2011 Petroleum Revenue Management Act set up stabilisation and heritage funds.

moses-smt-2007.summary: In 2007 the open-source Moses toolkit let any researcher train a statistical translation system from paired texts. It let researchers train translation systems from parallel corpora, large collections of texts paired with their human translations, and translate new sentences with those models, which put statistical translation within reach of labs that had never built their own.

chile-salmon-isa-crisis-2007.summary: In July 2007 Marine Harvest reported infectious salmon anaemia at a farm in Chiloé, Los Lagos region, and within two years the orthomyxovirus had reached most Atlantic salmon production areas. Chile had grown since the 1980s into the second-largest farmed salmon producer, with dense cages, shared fjords and heavy antibiotic use; Atlantic salmon harvests fell from around 400,000 tonnes in 2005 to roughly 100,000 tonnes by 2010, thousands of jobs were lost in Puerto Montt and Chiloé, and companies carried heavy debt. Chile's Congress amended its fisheries law in 2010 to create neighbourhood zoning, fallowing, density limits and sanitary controls; production recovered by 2014 under tighter oversight. The outbreak showed how single-species intensive farming could fail at scale.

chile-salmon-isa-crisis-2007.detail: First confirmation is dated to June or July 2007. ISA had struck Norway in 1984, Scotland in 1998 and Faroe Islands in 2000, with eradication via culling and fallowing. Chile's industry had added coho and trout, which resist ISAV, so total farmed salmonid output fell less than Atlantic salmon alone. Employment in Los Lagos dropped by an estimated 15,000 to 25,000 jobs, and Norwegian-owned firms took losses in subsidiaries.

digicel-png-mobile-2007.summary: Before 2007 state-owned Telikom PNG's B-Mobile served about 100,000 subscribers, mostly in Port Moresby and Lae, in a country of 6 million where fewer than 2 percent of people had a phone of any kind. Irish-owned Digicel, already operating across Caribbean, won a licence and launched in July 2007, building solar and diesel-powered towers in highlands and islands and selling cheap handsets and prepaid credit through village traders. Within three years it had over a million subscribers; by 2013 estimates put mobile penetration near 40 percent. Watson's Madang fieldwork and Foster's history document how phones reached villages before roads, electricity or banks, changing kin obligations, markets and courtship.

Mobile banking and health messaging followed. Similar rapid uptake occurred in Fiji, Samoa, Tonga and Vanuatu after Digicel entered those markets from 2006.

lorimer-burst-parkes-2007.summary: Searching 2001 survey data from CSIRO's Parkes 64-metre dish for pulsars toward Small Magellanic Cloud, student David Narkevic and Duncan Lorimer at West Virginia University, with Matthew Bailes and Maura McLaughlin, found a five-millisecond burst so bright and dispersed it must have come from far outside Milky Way. Science published it in November 2007. Scepticism followed, including man-made 'perytons' traced to a Parkes microwave oven in 2015, until further bursts at Parkes and other telescopes confirmed a new class. Such bursts, now called FRBs, are used to weigh intergalactic matter. Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes review discovery in 2024.

Tartan Racing, from Carnegie Mellon University and General Motors, won $2 million with Boss, a modified Chevrolet Tahoe; Stanford Racing finished second and Virginia Tech's Victor Tango third.

It is free for commercial and research use.

Its oil lies in pre-salt rock, trapped beneath salt up to 2,000 metres thick, which lies under up to 2,000 metres of water and several kilometres of seabed. Tupi, later renamed Lula, was described as the Western Hemisphere's largest discovery in 30 years and could raise Brazil's reserves by more than 40%.

agbogbloshie-ewaste-accra-2008.summary: By about 2008 a scrapyard beside Odaw river in central Accra, Ghana, was processing much of West Africa's discarded electronics. Young workers, many migrants from northern Ghana, burned cable insulation to recover copper and broke open monitors and refrigerators by hand, releasing lead, dioxins and brominated flame retardants into soil, smoke and Korle lagoon. Imports arrived as second-hand goods, a large share unusable. Sediment sampling found trace-metal contamination and health risks for workers, and Accra's waste system left recovery to informal networks. Photojournalists and Greenpeace made Agbogbloshie a global image of e-waste; later scholars call that image exaggerated.

Accra authorities demolished Agbogbloshie in 2021, which dispersed such work without ending it. australia-mandatory-internet-filter-2008.summary: Communications minister Stephen Conroy announced in December 2007 that internet service providers would be required to block a secret blacklist of 'refused classification' material for all Australians. Simpson's 2008 analysis placed proposal in Labor's electoral politics and religious lobbying; OpenNet Initiative's Access Denied compared it with filtering elsewhere. Trials in 2008-09 showed slowing and over-blocking; blacklist leaked in 2009 to include dentists and a tuckshop. Electronic Frontiers Australia, Google and Greens opposed. On 9 November 2012 Conroy abandoned legislation, relying instead on Interpol's child-abuse blocklist. Episode shaped later debates on eSafety powers and social media age limits.

Carr argued that online reading, which skips and skims, is shallower than sustained attention to print, and that internet use may erode our capacity for concentration and contemplation. He expanded it into his 2010 book The Shallows, which was a Pulitzer Prize finalist.

eskom-load-shedding-2008.summary: In January 2008 South Africa's state utility Eskom lost about 4,000 megawatts, roughly a tenth of its capacity, to wet coal stockpiles, maintenance backlogs and unplanned outages. Reserve margins fell from about ten percent to near zero and Eskom began scheduled rolling cuts it called load shedding, with a weekday shortfall near 3,500 megawatts. For several days it could not guarantee power to gold and platinum mines, which stopped production. Demand had grown since 1994, and a government decision in 2004 came too late to build new stations. Load shedding returned in 2014 and ran for a decade, reshaping South African investment in rooftop solar and batteries.

masdar-city-groundbreaking-2008.summary: In February 2008 Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company begins construction of Masdar City beside the emirate's airport: a 6 square kilometre district designed by Foster + Partners for 50,000 residents, powered by a 10 megawatt solar plant and rooftop panels, cooled by narrow shaded streets and a wind tower, and served by driverless pods instead of cars. Budget is put at 22 billion dollars and completion at 2016. First phase, Masdar Institute of Science and Technology with MIT, opens in 2010. After 2008 financial crisis targets slip: pods stop at one line, carbon-neutral goal is dropped in 2016 and population stays in low thousands. Masdar remains a test bed for desert building science and home of IRENA, and critics treat it as lesson in eco-city marketing.

svalbard-seed-vault-2008.summary: On 26 February 2008 Norway opens Svalbard Global Seed Vault, cut more than 100 meters into a mountain near Longyearbyen under 40 to 60 meters of rock and kept at minus 18 degrees Celsius, as backup for the world's genebanks. At opening it holds 268,000 distinct samples from over 100 countries, with capacity for 4.5 million. Run by Norway with the Nordic Genetic Resource Center and Crop Trust, it stores duplicates under black-box terms: depositors keep ownership and only they may withdraw. Westengen, Jeppson and Guarino counted 774,601 samples from 53 genebanks by 2013, over one third of distinct accessions held worldwide. On 14 October 2026 FAO reported 21 institutions depositing 16,676 samples, adding to more than 1.4 million already secured.

sources.title: Westengen, O. T., Jeppson, S. and Guarino, L., 'Global Ex-Situ Crop Diversity Conservation and the Svalbard Global Seed Vault: Assessing the Current Status', PLoS ONE 8:5 (2013), e64146

svalbard-seed-vault-2008.detail: Permafrost was meant to keep seeds frozen if power failed, but meltwater entered its entrance tunnel in 2016, prompting waterproofing works. It stores no GM seed under Norwegian law. A first withdrawal, by ICARDA to rebuild its collection displaced from Aleppo by Syria's war, came in 2015, with regrown seed redeposited from 2017. Crop Trust's Cary Fowler led the project. Deposits in October 2026 came from Italy, Portugal, Peru, South Africa, Ukraine and six CGIAR genebanks.

lagos-brt-lite-2008.summary: On 17 March 2008 Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority opened a bus rapid transit corridor along Ikorodu Road and Funsho Williams Avenue, 22 km from Mile 12 to CMS in Lagos Island, with about 65 percent of its length on segregated lanes. Built for about US$1.7 million per km, far below full BRT systems, it used a cooperative of existing operators running 220 buses under franchise. Within six months it had carried 29 million passengers, about 200,000 a day; fares fell by around 30 percent and journey times by 40 percent against danfo minibuses. Later corridors and Chinese-built buses followed.

In 2015 a Mile 12 to Ikorodu extension added 13.5 km, and Primero Transport Services took over operations with new Chinese buses.

google-app-engine-2008.summary: In April 2008 Google App Engine ran developers' web applications on Google's servers. Developers uploaded code and Google ran it across its own servers, isolating each application and adding capacity as traffic grew, so no one had to buy or manage machines. Its preview release came on 7 April 2008.

github-2008.summary: In 2008 GitHub put code hosting online with social features; it became the place most of the world's software is written. It added access control, bug tracking, feature requests, task management and wikis to Git's version control, so developers could store, manage and share code together. Microsoft announced on June 4, 2018 that it would buy GitHub for $7.5 billion; by January 2023 GitHub reported over 100 million developers and more than 420 million repositories.

ethiopia-commodity-exchange-2008.summary: Eleni Gabre-Madhin, an economist who had studied how grain traders in Ethiopia lacked trust, grades and price information, led design of a national exchange that rang its opening bell on 24 April 2008. ECX combined certified warehouses issuing electronic receipts, standard grades, an open-outcry floor backed by a clearing system, and price dissemination by SMS, rural electronic tickers and radio. Coffee trading became mandatory through ECX from 2008, followed by sesame and beans. Donors put in about US$24 million. By 2010 ECX had traded over US$1 billion without a payment default and was copied in several African countries.

ethiopia-commodity-exchange-2008.detail: ECX was registered in March 2008 and issued its first warehouse receipt on 18 April. Electronic receipts came from certified warehouses in coffee and sesame towns, trades settled through partner banks on a T+1 basis, and prices went out by SMS, IVR, radio and 20 rural electronic display boards. Specialty exporters argued mandatory coffee trading cut traceability for specialty growers, until a 2017 reform allowed direct sales.

foldit-2008.summary: In 2008 Foldit turned protein folding into an online game; in 2011 players deciphered a monkey virus enzyme's structure that had defied scientists for 15 years. Players fold protein structures as neatly as they can, and researchers analyze top solutions. Since 2008 it has competed in CASP, an international experiment scoring methods for predicting unknown protein structures.

wall-e-film-2008.summary: In June 2008 Pixar's WALL-E followed a lone robot cleaning an abandoned Earth for 700 years. It follows one lone trash-compacting robot left to clean abandoned, garbage-covered Earth in 2805, humanity having departed on giant spaceships 700 years earlier, until EVE, a probe robot, arrives to scan for life. WALL-E won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and received five further nominations.

app-store-2008.summary: In July 2008 Apple opened the App Store; outside developers could sell software to every iPhone, and a new industry of apps was born. By 2018 it offered over 2 million apps; Apple says it had paid developers over $320 billion by 2023 and listed 1.9 million apps in 2024.

turkish-dizi-arab-export-2008.summary: Saudi-owned MBC broadcasts Turkish drama Gümüş as Noor in Syrian colloquial Arabic dubbing through 2008, and its finale on 30 August draws an estimated 85 million viewers over 15 according to MBC's figures. Dubbing in Damascus rather than classical Arabic, slow romantic plots and a Muslim yet secular setting give Turkish 'dizi' an audience from Morocco to Gulf; tourism to Istanbul from Arab states doubles within two years. Turkish producers turn export into an industry worth hundreds of millions of dollars a year, second only to United States in television drama exports by late 2010s, with sales across Latin America and Balkans. Saudi and Egyptian clerics denounce series; Arab satellite channels pull Turkish content in 2018 amid political rifts, then resume.

zimbabwe-cholera-2008.summary: Cholera appeared in Chitungwiza and Harare in August 2008 as municipal water treatment failed for lack of chemicals, sewers broke and hospitals closed during hyperinflation and a disputed election. By June 2009 WHO counted 98,424 cases and 4,276 deaths in 55 of 62 districts, a case-fatality rate of 4.3 percent, several times the usual level for a treatable disease. Oral rehydration points, cross-border teams and a unity government's health ministry slowed transmission by early 2009. Oswell Masakure's history shows how government denial and politicisation delayed response, and how memory of 2008 shaped Zimbabwe's 2018 outbreak.

zimbabwe-cholera-2008.detail: Cholera reached South Africa's Limpopo province via Beitbridge. Water-chemical shortages at Morton Jaffray works outside Harare were a central cause named in reporting and studies. Harare's water authority had been taken over by central government in 2005, and chlorine stocks ran out as Zimbabwe dollar collapsed. Outbreak was declared a national emergency in December 2008. Masakure shows how state media blamed Western sanctions and biological warfare while clinics went unpaid.

beijing-tianjin-high-speed-rail-2008.summary: A week before Beijing Olympics, on 1 August 2008, Ministry of Railways opens a 117 km dedicated passenger line between Beijing South and Tianjin, cutting travel time to 30 minutes with CRH3 and CRH2C trainsets derived from Siemens and Kawasaki designs built under technology-transfer contracts. It carries about 16 million passengers in its first year. World Bank analysts Lawrence, Bullock and Liu describe standardised viaduct and slab-track designs, a state-financed rollout and construction costs around two thirds of European levels. Network length passes 42,000 km by end 2022, more than rest of world combined, reshaping intercity travel, property markets and debt at China State Railway Group.

Nine days after first beam came a magnet quench: superconducting magnets suddenly lost their superconductivity, releasing stored energy and damaging over 50 of them. Repairs delayed operation 14 months, to 20 November 2009.

rwanda-plastic-bag-ban-2008.summary: Law No. 57/2008 of 10 September 2008 prohibited making, importing, using or selling polythene bags across Rwanda, building on a 2004 ministerial instruction aimed at manufacturers. Customs officers confiscate bags at borders and airports, shops switched to paper and cloth, and monthly umuganda community work days clear litter. Fines run from 5,000 to 300,000 francs with possible jail for traders. Pritish Behuria's study contrasts Rwanda's strict enforcement with Kenya's slower route and Uganda's reversals under industry lobbying. In 2019 Law 17/2019 extended prohibition to single-use plastic items.

android-2008.summary: In 2008 Google gave Android free to any phone maker, and it now runs about seven in ten smartphones worldwide. HTC's Dream, Android's first phone, went on sale a month later. Google had acquired Android, Andy Rubin's startup, in July 2005. Since 2011 Android has been the most used smartphone operating system worldwide; it has the largest installed base of any operating system, with over three billion monthly active users.

spotify-launch-2008.summary: In October 2008 Spotify launched legal streaming of any song for a monthly fee; piracy fell and the album gave way to the playlist. Listeners could play songs free with advertisements, or pay for ad-free and offline listening; this freemium model offered an alternative to file sharing. By late 2025 it had 751 million monthly active users and 290 million paying subscribers.

Its public ledger, maintained by many computers checking each other's work, ensures each bitcoin can be spent only once, solving double-spending, which had defeated earlier digital cash. Nakamoto mined bitcoin's first block on 3 January 2009, and its use as currency began that year.

zimbabwe-hyperinflation-peak-2008.summary: After years of money printing to cover deficits, Zimbabwe's currency collapsed. Steve Hanke and Alex Kwok, using black-market exchange rates after official statistics stopped, estimate monthly inflation peaked at 79.6 billion percent in mid-November 2008, a daily rate near 98 percent with prices doubling every 24.7 hours, second only to Hungary in 1946. Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe issued a 100 trillion dollar note. Once the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange was shut in November 2008, trading in foreign currency became universal and prices stabilised; in January 2009 government legalised transactions in US dollars and rand. Shops, wages and even school fees moved to foreign money.

australia-nbn-2009.summary: In 2009 Australia announced a national broadband network to replace copper with fibre; a change of government cut it to a cheaper mix. It promised speeds up to 100 megabits per second. Cost estimates rose to A$43 billion before being revised to A$37.4 billion. After winning in 2013, Tony Abbott's Liberal-National coalition shifted to a cheaper multi-technology mix with 25 megabits as its minimum, and NBN Co declared its rollout complete in 2020.

imagenet-2009.summary: In 2009 Fei-Fei Li presented ImageNet, 14 million labelled photographs, the dataset that proved deep learning. Begun by Fei-Fei Li in 2006, it grew into more than 14 million photographs, each hand-labelled with what it shows, giving researchers far larger training and testing sets than before. Collaboration with PASCAL VOC's team led to ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge, which began in 2010 with 1,000 classes; AlexNet's 2012 win there set off deep learning's boom in vision.

india-groundwater-grace-2009.summary: Rodell, Velicogna and Famiglietti used NASA's GRACE gravity satellites to show that groundwater beneath Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana fell at 4 centimetres a year between 2002 and 2008, a loss of about 109 cubic kilometres, more than twice India's largest reservoir. Tiwari, Wahr and Swenson independently estimated 54 cubic kilometres a year across northern India and Bangladesh. Cause was pumping for irrigation by over 20 million electric and diesel wells, encouraged by free or subsidised farm power since Green Revolution, with no drop in rainfall. Findings put aquifer depletion at centre of Indian water policy and drove schemes for solar pumps, metering and crop diversification away from paddy in Punjab.

kazakhstan-top-uranium-producer-2009.summary: In 2009 Kazakhstan's mines produce about 14,000 tonnes of uranium, 28 percent of world output, passing Canada and Australia. Nearly all of it comes from in-situ leaching, in which acidified solution is pumped through sandstone ore bodies in Chu-Sarysu and Syrdarya basins and uranium is recovered at surface without open pits or shafts, a method Soviet geologists tested here from 1970. State company Kazatomprom develops deposits in joint ventures with Cameco, Areva, Uranium One and Chinese partners, opening mines such as Khorassan and Irkol in 2009 alone. Output doubles again by 2013 and country holds about 40 percent of world supply, so fuel for reactors from France to China depends on Kazakh wells, and Kazatomprom lists in London in 2018.

bitcoin-genesis-2009.summary: On 3 January 2009 Satoshi Nakamoto mined Bitcoin's first block, embedding that day's headline on bank bailouts. It carried “The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks,” that day's newspaper headline, proof it could not have been created earlier. Nine days later Hal Finney received bitcoin's first transaction, ten bitcoins from Nakamoto.

google-self-driving-car-2009.summary: In 2009 Google began building self-driving cars, the project that became Waymo, now carrying paying passengers. Google revealed it in October 2010; in December 2016 it became Waymo, which now runs paid robotaxi services in US cities.

omid-satellite-launch-2009.summary: On 2 February 2009, during celebrations of thirty years since Khomeini's return, a two-stage Safir rocket launched from Semnan desert carries Omid ('Hope'), a 27-kilogram cube built by Iran Electronics Industries for store-and-forward data relay, into an orbit of roughly 245 by 380 kilometres at 55 degrees inclination. US Strategic Command catalogues two objects and confirms orbit; Omid decays after about three months. Safir derives from Shahab-3 ballistic missiles, themselves descended from North Korean Nodong designs, so Western governments read this launch as a missile test as much as a civil milestone. Later Safir and Simorgh flights lift Rasad, Navid and, after many failures, Noor military satellites launched by Revolutionary Guards' Qased in 2020.

black-saturday-bushfires-victoria-2009.summary: On 7 February 2009, with Melbourne at 46.4 degrees and winds above 100 kilometres an hour, fires including Kilmore East and Murrindindi destroyed Marysville, Kinglake and other towns, killing 173 and destroying more than 2,000 homes. A royal commission's 2010 report questioned 'stay or go' policy, leading to a new Catastrophic fire danger rating, emergency warnings and buy-back of high-risk properties. Victoria's distributor SP AusNet settled a class action over a failed conductor at Kilmore East for almost 500 million dollars in 2014.

Some stations continued nightlight service for a while, and low-power broadcasting continued. Switching off analog freed channels 52 to 69, known as the 700 MHz band, which FCC had auctioned in 2008 for mobile services and reserved in part for police, fire and emergency communications.

easypaisa-pakistan-2009.summary: State Bank of Pakistan issues branchless banking regulations in April 2008 that let banks serve customers through agents. In October 2009 Tameer Microfinance Bank and its owner Telenor Pakistan launch Easypaisa: anyone, with or without a Telenor phone or bank account, can pay bills or send cash to another town by handing money to a shopkeeper agent who keys in a transaction. By July 2011 Easypaisa reports 23 million transactions worth about 500 million dollars through over 12,000 agents, mostly domestic remittances, far ahead of mobile wallet take-up. UBL Omni follows in 2010. This over-the-counter route differs from Kenya's wallet-based M-Pesa, and it defines Pakistani mobile finance for a decade.

Samsung supplied the GT-B3710 modem; Huawei provided network infrastructure in Oslo and Ericsson in Stockholm. LTE's design allows downloads of up to 300 megabits per second, far above 3G, though TeliaSonera branded it “4G” before ITU had defined that term.

koomeys-law-2010.summary: In 2010 Jonathan Koomey showed that computations per joule had doubled every 1.6 years for half a century. philippines-call-centre-lead-2010.summary: A Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas survey records 10.1 billion dollars of IT-BPO revenue and 536,128 employees in 2010, with contact centres employing about 350,000, more than India's estimated 330,000 voice agents. Growth from a few thousand seats in 2000 rested on American-accented English from a US-shaped school system, fibre links, tax holidays in PEZA buildings and night-shift work for clients such as JPMorgan and Convergys. Jan Padios's ethnography examines what it means to perform American customer service from Manila at night. By 2019 industry revenue exceeded 26 billion dollars and 1.3 million jobs, second only to remittances as foreign exchange source, and spawned Clark, Cebu and Davao office districts.

playpump-failure-2010.summary: PlayPumps International installed roundabouts that pumped borehole water into a 2,500-litre tank as children spun them, and won pledges of US$16.4 million in 2006 from the US government, Case Foundation and others for 4,000 units across Africa. Field reports from Mozambique by a Swiss water agency in 2008 and a UNICEF evaluation found children tired, women turning heavy wheels for hours, pumps idle for months awaiting repair and communities asking for their hand pumps back. Sponsors suspended funding in 2009, and in 2010 PlayPumps' sponsor handed remaining stock to Water For People. The case became a standard caution on untested aid technology.

Design derived from a South African advertising firm's idea in 1990s, with billboard space on tanks meant to fund maintenance. Cost near US$14,000 per unit compared with about US$3,000 for a hand pump, and installations on existing hand pump boreholes removed working pumps.

relu-2010.summary: In 2010 Nair and Hinton proposed the ReLU, an activation function that passes positive inputs through unchanged and outputs zero for negative ones. In 2011 Glorot's group described advantages over sigmoid and tanh, and found that deep networks trained with ReLU could perform strongly without unsupervised pre-training, especially on large supervised tasks. It avoids vanishing gradients and is now one of the most used activation functions.

burj-khalifa-opens-2010.summary: Emaar's tower, designed by Adrian Smith and structural engineer William Baker at Skidmore, Owings and Merrill and built by Samsung C&T with Besix and Arabtec, uses a Y-shaped 'buttressed core' in which three wings brace a hexagonal hub, confusing wind vortices as setbacks spiral upward. Crews pump high-strength concrete, cooled with ice and poured at night, to 606 metres, a record, before a steel spire takes it to 828 metres. Opened on 4 January 2010 and renamed from Burj Dubai for Abu Dhabi's ruler after a bailout during Dubai's debt crisis, it holds 163 floors, 57 lifts and a condensate system collecting 15 million gallons of water a year from air conditioning. Migrant workers paid a few dollars a day built it, and Burj's height exceeds Taipei 101 by 320 metres.

ipad-2010.summary: In 2010 Steve Jobs unveiled the iPad, and tablets became a screen for people who never wanted a computer. This tablet had a 9.7-inch touchscreen and ran iPhone software, positioned between phone and laptop. Its Wi-Fi model went on sale in America on April 3, 2010; 3 million sold in 80 days, and more than 15 million by iPad 2's launch.

bt-brinjal-moratorium-2010.summary: Genetic Engineering Approval Committee clears Mahyco's Bt brinjal, carrying Monsanto's Cry1Ac gene against fruit and shoot borer, on 14 October 2009, which would have made it India's first genetically modified food crop. Environment minister Jairam Ramesh holds public consultations in seven cities through January 2010 and on 9 February 2010 announces an indefinite moratorium, citing lack of scientific consensus, opposition from most brinjal-growing states, unanswered safety questions, negative public sentiment and brinjal's diversity in India. Shelton's 2010 commentary in Crop Protection criticises this reasoning; Bangladesh approves Bt brinjal in 2013 using Mahyco's event. India's moratorium still stands in 2026 and shapes its GM mustard debate.

ihub-nairobi-2010.summary: In March 2010 iHub opened in Nairobi as a shared workspace for developers. It was founded by Erik Hersman, Juliana Rotich, David Kobia and Ory Okolloh, who had built Ushahidi, with grants from Omidyar Network and Hivos. Members got mentoring, workshops and introductions to venture capital; Lagos-based Co-Creation Hub acquired it in September 2019.

Among its goals was giving at least 100 million American households access to connections of 100 megabits per second by 2020, alongside aims in health care, education, public safety and civic engagement.

nam-theun-2-dam-laos-2010.summary: Nam Theun 2 Power Company, owned by EDF, Electricity Generating of Thailand and Lao government, brings a 1,070 MW plant into commercial operation in April 2010 after 54 months of construction. Water from a 450 square kilometre reservoir on Nakai Plateau drops 350 metres to Xe Bang Fai basin; 995 MW is sold to Thailand under a 25-year agreement and 75 MW to Laos. World Bank, returning to large dams after a decade's pause, backed it in 2005 with guarantees tied to resettlement of about 6,300 people and a revenue management scheme for poverty programmes. Baird, Shoemaker and Manorom document downstream impacts on fisheries and livelihoods of tens of thousands along Xe Bang Fai that were less well addressed. Laos then pursued dozens of dams toward a 'battery of Southeast Asia' goal.

arabic-script-domain-names-2010.summary: Internet domain names had been limited to ASCII letters since DNS began in 1983; a Punycode encoding standardised in 2003 let browsers display Unicode labels but top-level domains stayed Latin. ICANN opens an expedited process for country-code domains in native scripts in November 2009, and on 5 May 2010 it adds مصر (Egypt), السعودية (Saudi Arabia) and امارات (Emirates) to root servers as first non-Latin top-level domains. Egypt's communications minister Tarek Kamel and Saudi Arabia's SaudiNIC had led technical work on Arabic script issues such as right-to-left rendering and variant letters. Russia's .рф follows a week later. Uptake stays modest, since most Arabic sites keep .com or ASCII country codes, but mixed-script addresses raise new phishing concerns.

Jeremy Sturdivant ordered pizzas from Papa John’s and had them delivered to Hanyecz, receiving bitcoin in return; bitcoin users commemorate it on May 22.

hayabusa-sample-return-2010.summary: Launched on an M-V rocket from Uchinoura on 9 May 2003, Hayabusa reaches 535 metre asteroid Itokawa in September 2005, touches down twice in November and loses fuel, attitude control and contact for weeks. Engineers at JAXA's Sagamihara campus nurse it home on microwave-discharge ion engines, cross-wiring parts of two failed units in 2009. On 13 June 2010 its capsule parachutes into Woomera Prohibited Area while main craft burns up. About 1,500 grains under 10 micrometres prove to be Itokawa material, and Tomoki Nakamura's team shows it matches LL ordinary chondrite meteorites, tying a meteorite class to a specific S-type asteroid.

stuxnet-2010.summary: In 2010 researchers found Stuxnet, first software built to wreck machines. Sergey Ulasen of Belarusian antivirus company VirusBlokAda uncovered this worm on 17 June. It targeted Siemens industrial control systems at Iran's uranium-enrichment plant at Natanz, making centrifuges spin themselves apart while reporting normal readings. The New York Times reported in 2012 that it was a joint US and Israeli operation.

openstack-2010.summary: On 20 July 2010 Rackspace announced OpenStack, backed by NASA, free software for running your own cloud from any vendor's hardware. It pools processing, storage and networking from hardware of many vendors and lets users rent virtual servers from that pool, inside one company or as a public cloud. Early code came from NASA's Nebula platform and Rackspace's Cloud Files; a nonprofit foundation took over OpenStack in September 2012.

Aadhaar is a 12-digit number linked to a photograph, ten fingerprints and two iris scans, stored in one central database run by UIDAI, set up in January 2009. In September 2018, India's Supreme Court upheld the Aadhaar Act while restricting some mandatory uses.

haiti-cholera-un-peacekeepers-2010.summary: In mid-October 2010, nine months after Haiti's earthquake, cholera cases appeared along Artibonite river downstream of a MINUSTAH camp at Mirebalais housing Nepalese troops, in a country with no recorded cholera for a century. Epidemiologist Renaud Piarroux's team mapped early cases to the camp's sewage, and whole-genome sequencing showed Haitian isolates nearly identical to 2010 Nepalese Vibrio cholerae. By 2016 more than 788,000 people had fallen ill and over 9,000 had died; United Nations, which had resisted the link, acknowledged a role in December 2016 under Ban Ki-moon and apologised. Vaccination, water and sanitation drives ended transmission in 2019, but cholera returned in 2022. The outbreak reshaped peacekeeper health screening and debates on UN legal immunity.

haiti-cholera-un-peacekeepers-2010.detail: Ban's apology came on 1 December 2016. Within weeks of October 2010 cholera reached all ten departments, with case fatality above 4 percent at first; Partners In Health and Cuban medical brigades treated tens of thousands. Lawsuits in US courts were dismissed on immunity grounds in 2016. UN pledged 400 million dollars for a victims' fund but raised a fraction. Haiti's own water systems had been underfunded for decades before the earthquake.

instagram-2010.summary: In October 2010 Instagram launched on the iPhone, photos with filters and nothing else; it gained 25,000 users the first day. Users posted square photographs dressed up with filters; it reached 1 million registered users in two months and 10 million within a year. Facebook bought it in April 2012 for about $1 billion, and it passed 1 billion users in June 2018.

copiapo-san-jose-mine-rescue-2010.summary: On 5 August 2010 a collapse sealed 33 miners 700 metres down in San José copper and gold mine in Chile's Atacama region. They rationed two days of food over 17 days until a percussion drill broke into their refuge on 22 August and brought up a note, 'Estamos bien en el refugio los 33'. Codelco engineers under minister Laurence Golborne ran three parallel drilling plans; Plan B, a Schramm T130 rig with Center Rock downhole hammers operated by Chilean and American crews, reached them on 9 October. On 13 October Fénix 2, a capsule, built by Chilean navy shipyard ASMAR with NASA advice, lifted all 33 in under 24 hours before an estimated billion television viewers. Studies by Useem and Edmondson treat this operation as a case in crisis leadership.

Supplies went down a 12-centimetre borehole in 'paloma' tubes. Inquiries found owner San Esteban Primera had ignored safety orders; Chile ratified ILO Convention 176 on mine safety in 2013. Rescue costs reached about 20 million dollars.

deepmind-founded-2010.summary: In 2010 DeepMind was founded in London, incorporated on 23 September and named DeepMind Technologies on 15 November, to build machines that learn anything, the lab behind AlphaGo and AlphaFold. Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman set out to build general-purpose learning systems. Google bought it in January 2014 for a reported $400 million to $650 million. Its AlphaGo program beat Go world champion Lee Sedol in 2016, and its AlphaFold set records in protein structure prediction in 2020; in April 2023 it merged with Google Brain to form Google DeepMind.

kinect-2010.summary: In November 2010 Microsoft's Kinect tracked players' bodies with a depth camera; robotics labs bought it for $150 as a cheap 3D sensor. This Xbox 360 add-on used a camera and infrared depth sensor to track players' bodies, so they controlled games with movement and no handheld controller, unlike Nintendo's Wii Remote. It sold an estimated eight million units in its first 60 days, a Guinness World Record for fastest-selling consumer electronics device; robotics researchers also adopted its depth sensing widely.

psa-kiwifruit-canker-new-zealand-2010.summary: Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae was confirmed in Bay of Plenty on 5 November 2010. Virulent strain spread to most orchards within three years, devastating gold cultivar Hort16A, on which Zespri's premium exports rested. Vanneste's 2017 Annual Review of Phytopathology account estimates costs near 900 million New Zealand dollars and traces likely origin to imported pollen or plant material; his 2010 and 2012 papers characterised strains. Growers cut out Hort16A and grafted Gold3 (SunGold), bred by Plant and Food Research, which proved tolerant; industry exceeded pre-Psa earnings by 2016. Growers' negligence suit against Ministry for Primary Industries succeeded at first instance in 2018 but was overturned on appeal.

pike-river-mine-explosion-2010.summary: Pike River Coal's underground mine near Greymouth exploded at 3:44 pm on 19 November 2010; two men walked out, 29 remained and three further explosions ended rescue hopes. Royal commission of 2012 found company had pursued production before ventilation and gas-drainage systems were ready, with a single egress and ignored methane alarms, while Department of Labour inspectors lacked capacity. Wilson's 2012 casebook and Logan, Cavana and Howell's 2025 systems study analyse drift into failure. Reforms created WorkSafe New Zealand in 2013 and Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. A re-entry of drift from 2019 to 2021 recovered evidence but no bodies.

menafrivac-2010.summary: Epidemics of group A meningococcal meningitis swept the Sahel belt from Senegal to Ethiopia every few years; the 2009 season caused about 88,000 cases and 5,000 deaths. After African health ministers rejected a vaccine priced for rich markets, a Meningitis Vaccine Project set up by PATH and WHO in 2001 with 70 million dollars in Gates Foundation money contracted the Serum Institute of India to make a conjugate vaccine for under 50 US cents a dose. Trials from 2005 in The Gambia, Ghana, India, Mali and Senegal showed stronger antibody responses than older polysaccharide vaccines. Burkina Faso began vaccinating first, in December 2010, reaching 12 million people aged 1 to 29 in weeks. Group A cases fell by more than 99 percent in vaccinated areas, and no group A epidemic has occurred there since.

US and Japanese deliveries began in December 2010. Its first version went about 160 km on one charge; it was the world's best-selling plug-in electric car until Tesla's Model 3 passed it in early 2020, with 577,000 sold by February 2022.

arab-spring-social-media-2011.summary: In 2011 protesters across the Arab world used Facebook and Twitter; rulers fell in Tunisia and Egypt. Those uprisings began in Tunisia in late 2010, after Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire, and spread in 2011. Facebook and Twitter helped Egyptian and Tunisian activists coordinate protests and circulate information, though social-media use rose after protests began; nine in ten Egyptians and Tunisians polled said they used Facebook to organize protests or spread awareness. Social media contributed to those uprisings but did not cause them alone.

brown-v-ema-2011.summary: In June 2011 the Supreme Court ruled video games are protected speech like books and films; states could not ban their sale to minors. In Brown v. Entertainment Merchants Association it struck down California's 2005 law AB 1179, sponsored by state senator Leland Yee, which banned selling violent video games to anyone under 18 and required labels beyond ESRB ratings. Justices voted 7 to 2 to nullify that law under the First Amendment.

kudankulam-protests-2011.summary: Two Russian VVER-1000 reactors at Kudankulam on Tamil Nadu's southern coast near completion when Fukushima melts down in March 2011. From August 2011 People's Movement Against Nuclear Energy, led by S. P. Udayakumar and based in Idinthakarai, a fishing village beside the site, holds relay hunger strikes, sea blockades and marches by thousands, mostly fishing families and women. Police file sedition cases against thousands and charge protesters in September 2012. Supreme Court clears the plant on 6 May 2013 with safety conditions; unit one reaches criticality on 13 July 2013 and joins the grid on 22 October 2013. Kaur's 2020 ethnography treats Kudankulam as a study in how coastal communities weigh nuclear risk against livelihoods.

turkle-alone-together-2011.summary: In January 2011 Sherry Turkle argued from 450 interviews that we expect more from technology and less from each other. Drawing on interviews with 450 people, the MIT psychologist argued that our “always-on connectivity culture” leaves people confused about whether they have each other's attention, and that social robots are no substitute for human contact, writing that “Humans need to be surrounded by human touch, faces, and voices.” She called for a correction in how people use technology.

tunisia-uprising-social-media-2011.summary: On 17 December 2010 street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi set himself alight in Sidi Bouzid after police confiscated his cart. Protests spread town by town, recorded on phones and shared on Facebook, where state censors had left access open, then relayed by Al Jazeera and bloggers. Within four weeks, on 14 January 2011, President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali fled to Saudi Arabia after 23 years in power. On Twitter, activists, journalists and ordinary users formed a symbiotic news system that amplified events to a global audience. Tunisia's uprising opened the Arab Spring and set a template for networked protest in Egypt days later.

egypt-internet-shutdown-2011.summary: In January 2011 Egypt switched off its internet for five days to stifle protests, and the regime fell within weeks. About 93% of Egyptian networks became unreachable. All four providers restored connectivity on 2 February 2011 on Mubarak's order. Censorship and surveillance later increased after Mohamed Morsi's 2013 overthrow, and Freedom House downgraded Egypt's internet from “partly free” to “not free”.

brazil-oxitec-gm-mosquito-release-2011.summary: From February 2011 researchers from Universidade de São Paulo, Moscamed Brasil and UK firm Oxitec released OX513A male Aedes aegypti in Itaberaba and then Juazeiro, Bahia, under approval from biosafety commission CTNBio. Their strain carries a tetracycline-repressible lethal gene so offspring die as larvae; sustained releases of millions of males in Mandacaru and Juazeiro districts reduced wild larval numbers by 81 to 95 percent. CTNBio approved commercial release in April 2014 and Oxitec built a production plant in Piracicaba, while regulators withheld registration for years and critics questioned long-term suppression and gene persistence. Brazil became the main testing ground for genetically engineered insect control against dengue, Zika and chikungunya vectors.

brazil-oxitec-gm-mosquito-release-2011.detail: A 2019 study found OX513A-derived genes in wild mosquitoes at Jacobina after releases there; Oxitec disputed that reading, and Scientific Reports attached an editorial expression of concern. Earlier trials ran in Cayman Islands in 2009 to 2010. Oxitec, spun out of Oxford University in 2002, bred mosquitoes in a Juazeiro facility and released about 400,000 males a week at peak. IBM announced Watson's first commercial use in 2013, for lung cancer treatment decisions at Memorial Sloan Kettering, and spun off Watson Health in 2022.

christchurch-earthquake-2011.summary: At 12:51 pm on 22 February 2011 a shallow magnitude 6.2 aftershock of September 2010 Darfield earthquake struck beneath Christchurch's southeastern suburbs. Instruments near its source recorded vertical accelerations above 2 g, among highest ever measured in a city. Canterbury Television and Pyne Gould buildings collapsed, killing 133 of 185 dead; unreinforced masonry fell on streets. Liquefaction ejected sand and water across eastern suburbs, wrecking foundations and pipes; government later red-zoned about 8,000 residential properties as unrebuildable. Light timber-framed houses performed well structurally but suffered from ground failure. Royal Commission's 2012 report drove changes to building assessment, unreinforced masonry rules and engineering oversight.

christchurch-earthquake-2011.detail: Central business district stayed cordoned for over two years and roughly 70 percent of its buildings were demolished. Insurance claims exceeded 40 billion New Zealand dollars, among costliest disasters relative to GDP. Rebuild introduced base-isolated buildings and low-damage design. Red zone along Avon River became a regeneration area with wetlands. Port Hills rockfall led to further property purchases. Earthquake Commission reforms followed in 2019.

fukushima-nuclear-accident-2011.summary: In 2011 a tsunami cut power to Fukushima Daiichi, three reactors melted down, and 164,000 people fled. The accident in Ōkuma, Japan, turned Germany and others against nuclear power. The Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami knocked out grid power and nearly all backup power, so reactors could not be cooled after shutdown; fuel overheated, hydrogen explosions damaged reactor buildings, and radioactive material escaped. At least 164,000 residents were displaced, and investigations faulted lapses in safety and oversight, including risk assessment and evacuation planning.

iron-dome-2011.summary: In April 2011 Iron Dome shot down its first rocket over Ashkelon; radar and software decided within seconds which rockets to hit. Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and Israel Aerospace Industries developed this mobile system to destroy short-range rockets and shells fired from 4 to 70 kilometres away whose path threatens populated areas. In March 2012 The Jerusalem Post reported it downing 90% of such rockets, and by late 2014 it had intercepted over 1,200.

filter-bubble-2011.summary: In 2011 Eli Pariser argued that personalised feeds show each person a different world, a hypothesis later studies found little evidence for. Such systems tailor results to each person's location, clicks and search history. He described two people searching Google for “BP”: one got investment news, one got news of BP's Deepwater Horizon oil spill. Filtered results, he argued, give people less exposure to conflicting viewpoints and close them off from new ideas.

bkash-mobile-money-2011.summary: bKash, a subsidiary of BRAC Bank founded by Kamal and Iqbal Quadir with Money in Motion, launched in July 2011 under Bangladesh Bank's 2011 mobile financial services guidelines. Customers open wallets with basic phones using USSD menus and cash in or out at small shop agents. By 2014 it had 15 million accounts and over 100,000 agents, carrying garment wages, remittances from city to village and bill payments where bank branches were scarce. bushehr-nuclear-grid-2011.summary: Bushehr Unit 1 connects to Iran's grid on 3 September 2011, first power reactor in region. Siemens's KWU began two pressurised-water units on Gulf coast in 1975 for Shah's government, abandoned them after 1979, and Iraqi bombing damaged shells during 1980s war. A January 1995 contract with Russia's Atomstroyexport fitted a VVER-1000 of 915 megawatts net into German containment, a hybrid that took 16 years, repeated fuel delays and a 2010 Stuxnet episode at Natanz to finish. Russia supplies fuel and takes back spent fuel under IAEA safeguards, an arrangement cited in later nonproliferation debates. Commercial operation follows in September 2013, and two further Russian units start construction in 2019 amid sanctions.

thailand-floods-hdd-2011.summary: Monsoon rains and dam releases in 2011 sent Chao Phraya floodwaters over seven industrial estates in Ayutthaya and Pathum Thani during October and November, submerging plants of Western Digital, Toshiba, Nidec and hundreds of suppliers that together made about 40 percent of world's hard disk drives and most of their spindle motors. Global drive shipments fell by roughly a quarter in following quarter, prices doubled, and PC makers from Japan to United States cut output. Haraguchi and Lall's study traces how concentration of a single component in one flood plain propagated losses through global supply chains, and World Bank put total damage and losses at about 1.4 trillion baht (US$46 billion).

Siri came out of SRI International's Artificial Intelligence Center and DARPA's CALO project, and shipped as a standalone iPhone app in 2010. Apple bought it two months later and removed that app from the App Store once Siri was built into iPhone.

nest-learning-thermostat-2011.summary: On 25 October 2011 Nest Labs, founded in May 2010 by former Apple executives Tony Fadell and Matt Rogers, unveils its Nest Learning Thermostat at 249 dollars, about five times a Honeywell Round's price. A steel ring and colour display replace the beige box; motion sensors switch to auto-away, Wi-Fi allows control from a phone, and after a week it builds its own schedule from temperatures its owners choose. Heating and cooling take about half of a home's energy, and Nest claimed savings of up to 30 per cent. Pre-orders opened at Best Buy and Nest.com with shipping in mid-November. Google bought Nest in 2014, and the thermostat became the template for smart-home devices.

Short guide RNA steers Cas9, an enzyme, to cut DNA at a chosen site; earlier tools such as zinc finger nucleases and TALENs required one custom protein per target, so CRISPR was far easier to design. In October 2020, Doudna and Charpentier received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for it.

dropout-2014.summary: In 2012 Hinton's group introduced dropout, its journal paper following in 2014. Dropout fights overfitting, where networks memorize training data instead of learning patterns that generalize, by randomly switching off neurons in training so none can rely on another or settle into brittle combinations; at test time an unthinned network with scaled-down weights is used. Google holds a patent on this technique.

era-deep.summary: From 2012, after contest wins from 2009 to 2011, deep neural networks trained on big data with graphics chips beat every other method, and AI research reorganised around them after that year's ImageNet result. Access to big data, cheaper and faster computers and advanced machine learning techniques together improved image and video processing, text analysis and speech recognition over the following years.

Work showed deterministic placement of individual atoms, about a decade ahead of industry roadmaps, and underpinned Silicon Quantum Computing, a company Simmons founded in 2017. ska-site-decision-murchison-2012.summary: After a decade of competition, SKA Organisation's members announced on 25 May 2012 that Square Kilometre Array radio telescope would be built in two countries. South Africa's Karoo would host mid-frequency dishes and Australia's Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory, on Wajarri Yamaji land 800 kilometres north of Perth, would host low-frequency antennas and survey dishes. Site evaluation committee had ranked South Africa slightly higher; compromise kept both consortia and their precursor telescopes, MeerKAT and ASKAP, within project. Murchison was chosen for radio quietness protected by Australian regulation, as Wilson, Storey and Tzioumis describe. Construction of SKA-Low's 131,072 antennas began in 2022 with first images in 2025.

A 2022 Indigenous Land Use Agreement with Wajarri Yamaji gave site its name Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara. SKA Observatory, an intergovernmental body, formed in 2021 with headquarters at Jodrell Bank. Full operation is planned for about 2030.

tesla-model-s-2012.summary: In June 2012 Tesla delivered Model S, its second vehicle after its Roadster, an electric car with an EPA-rated range of 265 miles in its 85 kWh version; Tesla planned to build 5,000 cars that year. It won Motor Trend's Car of the Year in 2013 and was 2015's best-selling plug-in electric vehicle worldwide.

three-gorges-dam-2012.summary: In July 2012 the Three Gorges Dam ran at full power, the largest power station on Earth; 1.3 million people had been moved for it. Spanning Yangtze River in Hubei province, central China, it has an installed capacity of 22,500 MW, making it Earth's largest power station by that measure; it also improves river shipping and controls floods on Yangtze Plain. Its construction displaced an estimated 1.13 to 1.4 million people.

india-blackout-2012.summary: On 30 July 2012 India's Northern Grid failed, and on 31 July Northern, Eastern and North-Eastern grids collapsed together, cutting supply to 22 states and over 600 million people, largest blackout by population on record. Trains stopped, miners were trapped and hospitals ran on diesel. An enquiry committee blamed overdrawal by states in a weak monsoon, a tripped 400 kV Bina-Gwalior line, inadequate protection and defiance of load despatch instructions. Restoration took hours to a day using hydro black start. Afterwards India synchronised all five regional grids into one national grid by December 2013, tightened grid discipline and expanded transmission.

curiosity-rover-2012.summary: In August 2012 Curiosity landed on Mars lowered by a rocket crane; the car-sized rover found evidence of an ancient lake. Its landing site was later named Bradbury Landing. Its goals included judging whether Gale ever offered conditions favorable to microbial life. Within about one year it had assessed that ancient Mars could have been hospitable to microbes, and it continues to operate more than a decade past its planned mission of one Martian year.

Hackers calling themselves Cutting Sword of Justice claimed responsibility; that year's attack displayed a burning US flag. Recovery took over one week and required replacing hard drives; Qatar's RasGas was hit soon after.

voyager-interstellar-2012.summary: In August 2012 Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space, 35 years after launch; it still reports from beyond the Sun's wind. That boundary is where our Sun's outflowing solar wind gives way to gas between stars. Voyager 1 remains Earth's most distant human-made object, and two of its instruments still operate.

Eighty-eight percent said robots are needed for jobs too hard or dangerous for people, and 60 percent wanted them banned from caring for children, elderly or disabled people.

mers-coronavirus-identified-2012.summary: In June 2012 a 60-year-old man dies of pneumonia and kidney failure at Dr Soliman Fakeeh Hospital in Jeddah. Virologist Ali Mohamed Zaki cultures sputum on Vero cells, finds a cytopathic effect no routine test explains and sends samples to Ron Fouchier's laboratory at Erasmus MC in Rotterdam, which sequences a betacoronavirus related to bat viruses, and Zaki posts a notice on ProMED-mail on 20 September 2012. Saudi authorities object to export of samples and Zaki leaves his post. Named Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus in 2013, it passes from dromedary camels to humans and spreads in hospitals; by 2024 WHO counts about 2,600 cases and 940 deaths, mostly in Saudi Arabia, with a 2015 outbreak of 186 cases in South Korea. Its study prepares laboratories for SARS-CoV-2.

alexnet-2012.summary: In 2012 AlexNet won the ImageNet contest by a margin that convinced researchers deep neural networks work. AlexNet won with a top-5 error rate of 15.3%, beating second place by more than 10.8 percentage points. Eight layers deep, this convolutional neural network sorts images into 1,000 categories and owed its accuracy to that depth, which made training costly; its team split it across two Nvidia GTX 580 GPUs. Its win pushed neural networks to the center of computer vision research.

m-kopa-pay-as-you-go-solar-2012.summary: On 19 October 2012 M-KOPA, founded in Nairobi by Jesse Moore and Nick Hughes, launched with Safaricom a d.light solar home system that customers switch on by paying 40 Kenyan shillings a day through M-PESA after a 2,500 shilling deposit. A SIM card inside each unit reports payments and switches power on or off, turning a 200 dollar product into a year of small instalments for households without grid connections. Three bulbs and phone charging replaced kerosene lamps. By 2016 M-KOPA had sold more than 300,000 systems in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. This coupling of cheap photovoltaics, efficient LEDs and mobile money opened a distinct path to electricity access.

The Economist named it after SunPower founder Richard Swanson in a late-2012 article that compared it to Moore's law. Crystalline silicon cell prices fell from $76.67 per watt in 1977 to $0.36 per watt in 2014.

murray-darling-basin-plan-2012.summary: Made under Water Act 2007 after Millennium Drought, Basin Plan set sustainable diversion limits for Australia's largest river system, requiring recovery of 2,750 gigalitres a year for environment through buybacks and infrastructure, with a possible 450 gigalitres more. A 2010 draft guide provoked burning of documents in Griffith; Grafton's 2011 chapter weighed economic costs and benefits. Implementation brought allegations of water theft exposed in 2017, mass fish kills at Menindee in 2019 and 2023, and a 2023 amendment extending deadlines. Noble, Guillaume and Wyborn consider uncertainty in diversion limits ahead of 2026 review.

north-korea-unha-3-satellite-2012.summary: On 12 December 2012 an Unha-3 three-stage rocket lifts off from Sohae station near Tongchang-ri and puts a 100 kg Kwangmyongsong-3 Unit 2 satellite into a sun-synchronous orbit, eight months after an April attempt broke up over Yellow Sea. US and South Korean tracking confirm an object in orbit, though no signal is ever received and analysts conclude it tumbled without functioning. Because Unha shares staging and engines with long-range ballistic missile programmes, UN Security Council Resolution 2087 of 22 January 2013 condemns launch and expands sanctions. North Korea's National Aerospace Development Administration, formed 2013, later launched Kwangmyongsong-4 in 2016 and a reconnaissance satellite in 2023.
