pakistan-polio-workers-killed-2012.summary: On 17 and 18 December 2012 gunmen shoot dead vaccinators in Karachi and Peshawar during a national polio immunisation round; within three days eight workers, most of them women, are killed. WHO and UNICEF suspend fieldwork and provincial governments stop campaigns. Attacks follow a Taliban ban on vaccination in North Waziristan from June 2012 and revelations that CIA had run a fake vaccination drive in Abbottabad in 2011 while hunting Osama bin Laden. Pakistan, with Afghanistan and Nigeria, is one of three countries where wild poliovirus still circulates; cases rise to 306 in 2014. Gulland's BMJ reports record these deaths and their effect on eradication, and vaccinators continue under police escort through following years.

ahmedabad-heat-action-plan-2013.summary: In May 2010 temperatures in Ahmedabad reach 46.8 degrees Celsius and all-cause mortality rises at least 30 percent above normal, about 1,344 excess deaths by later analysis. Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation works with Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar, NRDC and others on a heat action plan piloted in 2013: seven-day temperature forecasts trigger four colour-coded alerts, hospitals and community health workers are trained to recognise heat illness, water and shade are provided at public sites, and outreach warns slum residents and outdoor workers. Later evaluations estimate over a thousand deaths avoided a year, and India's disaster authority spreads similar plans to over a hundred cities.

dqn-atari-2013.summary: In 2013 DeepMind trained one network to play seven Atari games from screen pixels, beating earlier methods on six and a human expert on three. In reinforcement learning, software learns by trial and error from rewards; here each game's score was its reward and its input was four 84×84 frames. A 2015 Nature paper extended this to 49 games, one architecture learning all of them with minimal prior knowledge, beating competing methods on almost all and matching or surpassing a professional human game tester.

ebola-west-africa-2013.summary: In 2013 Ebola broke out in Guinea and spread across West Africa, killing 11,323, the largest outbreak ever. WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 8 August 2014, and declared it over on 9 June 2016 after later flare-ups. By May 2016 it counted 28,646 suspected cases and 11,323 deaths. In December 2016 WHO reported that trials of its rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine appeared to protect against this strain.

word2vec-2013.summary: In 2013 Google's Word2Vec turned words into vectors in which king minus man plus woman equals queen. It trains shallow two-layer neural networks to represent each word as a vector of numbers that captures its meaning from the words around it, so words used in similar ways end up close together. Their first paper described the continuous bag-of-words and skip-gram architectures; a follow-up added negative sampling, subsampling of frequent words and multi-word phrases. Trained embeddings became standard inputs for language systems.

Its browser-based design tool offers templates for presentations, posters and social media posts, plus photo and video editing. Melanie Perkins began it in 2012 in her mother's living room; it launched publicly in August 2013, passed 750,000 users in its first year, and was valued at US$40 billion at its 2021 peak.

After a lithium-ion battery fire on a parked Japan Airlines 787 in Boston and an ANA 787 emergency landing, the FAA grounded US 787s on 16 January. By next day all 50 delivered 787s worldwide were grounded, and Boeing halted deliveries until its battery system was redesigned. FAA let US 787s fly again on April 19, 2013.

angkor-lidar-survey-2013.summary: In April 2012 a helicopter carrying a Leica ALS60 laser scanner flies 370 square kilometres over Angkor, Phnom Kulen and Koh Ker for a consortium led by Damian Evans with APSARA Authority and École française d'Extrême-Orient. Ground returns filtered from billions of pulses show, in a 2013 PNAS paper, a formal grid of streets, canals, ponds and mounds around Angkor Wat and Angkor Thom and, under jungle on Phnom Kulen, a planned urban layout matching Mahendraparvata, Jayavarman II's ninth-century capital. Findings confirm a low-density city far larger than its walled core and support arguments that water-management strain and climate shifts contributed to Angkor's decline. A 2015 campaign extended coverage to 1,900 square kilometres.

novartis-glivec-judgment-2013.summary: When India amends its Patents Act in 2005 to allow drug product patents under WTO rules, Parliament adds Section 3(d): a new form of a known substance is not patentable unless it shows enhanced efficacy. Patent office refuses in 2006; after seven years of litigation Supreme Court rules on 1 April 2013 that efficacy means therapeutic efficacy and better bioavailability alone does not qualify. Gabble and Kohler's 2014 analysis in Globalization and Health weighs effects on access and research; generic makers keep supplying imatinib across low-income countries.

rana-plaza-collapse-2013.summary: On 24 April 2013 an eight storey building in Savar, outside Dhaka, housing five garment factories collapsed, killing 1,134 people and injuring over 2,500. Cracks had appeared a day earlier; shops and a bank closed but factory managers ordered workers back. Upper floors were added illegally on a structure built for shops, and heavy generators shook it. Victims were mostly young women sewing for European and North American brands. Within weeks over 200 brands signed Accord on Fire and Building Safety, a legally binding inspection regime, and others formed Alliance; thousands of factories were inspected and remediated. Bangladesh raised minimum wage and amended labour law; compensation was slow.

ranbaxy-guilty-plea-2013.summary: On 13 May 2013 Ranbaxy USA, arm of India's largest generic drugmaker, pleads guilty in Maryland federal court to seven felony counts and agrees to 500 million dollars in fines, forfeiture and civil settlement. Prosecutors show adulterated batches of acne drug Sotret, gabapentin and ciprofloxacin from Paonta Sahib in 2005 and 2006, and false stability test dates for antibiotics from Dewas reported to FDA in 2006 and 2007, with tests run months late or on one day and samples kept in a non-compliant refrigerator. Whistleblower Dinesh Thakur, a former executive, receives 48.6 million dollars. FDA import alerts on Ranbaxy plants follow; Sun Pharma buys Ranbaxy in 2014. Regulators and buyers tighten scrutiny of generic manufacturing data worldwide.

nicaragua-canal-hknd-2013.summary: On 13 June 2013 Nicaragua's National Assembly passed Law 840 granting Hong Kong Nicaragua Canal Development Group, led by telecoms entrepreneur Wang Jing, a 50-year renewable concession to build and run a canal from Brito on Pacific coast to Punta Gorda on Caribbean, about 278 kilometres through Lake Nicaragua, priced near 40 to 50 billion dollars. Scientists led by Jorge Huete-Pérez and Axel Meyer warned that dredging and salt intrusion threatened Central America's largest freshwater lake and ten percent of national territory, while farmers along the route protested expropriation terms. A ceremony marked a start in December 2014, but no construction followed; Wang lost most of his fortune in 2015, and on 8 May 2024 the Assembly repealed Law 840.

argentina-vaca-muerta-shale-2013.summary: On 16 July 2013 state-controlled YPF, renationalised a year earlier, signed with Chevron a 1.24 billion dollar first-phase agreement to drill Loma Campana in Neuquén, first large-scale development of Vaca Muerta, a Jurassic shale formation that US Energy Information Administration ranked second worldwide for recoverable shale gas and fourth for shale oil. Decree 929/2013 offered export and currency concessions to attract such investment. Horizontal wells and multistage hydraulic fracturing, adapted from Texas and North Dakota practice, raised Neuquén output; by 2024 Vaca Muerta supplied more than half of Argentine oil, with pipelines to Atlantic coast and plans for LNG exports. Mapuche communities and towns such as Añelo contested water use, seismicity and waste, while governments relied on the play for energy trade balance.

disi-water-conveyance-jordan-2013.summary: King Abdullah II inaugurates Disi Water Conveyance Project on 17 July 2013. Fifty-five wells in Disi-Mudawwara sandstone aquifer near Saudi border, shared with Saudi Arabia, feed 100 million cubic metres a year through a 325 kilometre pipeline climbing to Amman, raising capital's supply by about a third. Turkish contractor GAMA builds and operates it under a 25-year concession costing about 1 billion dollars with US and multilateral finance. In 2009 Duke University geochemists had reported radium in Disi groundwater at levels many times above international drinking guidance, forcing Jordan to blend and monitor supply. Aquifer is non-renewable, so project buys decades, not a solution, and a Red Sea desalination scheme is planned to follow.

colombia-onchocerciasis-elimination-2013.summary: On 29 July 2013 World Health Organization verified that Colombia had eliminated transmission of Onchocerca volvulus, parasite carried by Simulium blackflies that causes river blindness. Its single focus, 1,366 people in and around Naicioná on Río Micay in Cauca department, had received ivermectin donated by Merck twice a year from 1996 with coverage above 85 percent; transmission stopped by 2007, treatments ended in 2008 and three years of surveillance found no infected flies or children. Under Onchocerciasis Elimination Program for the Americas, Ecuador followed in 2014, Mexico in 2015 and Guatemala in 2016, leaving only a Yanomami focus on Venezuela-Brazil border. Colombia's case showed that mass drug administration alone could end transmission where foci are small and isolated.

colombia-onchocerciasis-elimination-2013.detail: Afro-Colombian community health workers carried out distribution in a conflict zone. Onchocerciasis arrived in the Americas with enslaved Africans and persisted in 13 foci in six countries; Simulium exiguum carried it in Colombia. Merck's Mectizan donation from 1987 and Carter Center coordination from 1996 let programmes treat twice yearly rather than once, which hastens interruption. Transmission in Americas fell sharply from 1995 to 2016.

hyperloop-concept-2013.summary: In August 2013 Elon Musk published a white paper for Hyperloop, capsules in low-pressure tubes from Los Angeles to the Bay Area. It proposed pressurized passenger capsules riding on air bearings through reduced-pressure tubes, driven by linear induction motors, with an example route from Los Angeles to the San Francisco Bay Area along Interstate 5. Hyperloop One declared bankruptcy and ceased operations on 31 December 2023, while other companies continued developing Hyperloop technology.

nokia-microsoft-2013.summary: In September 2013 Microsoft bought Nokia's phone business for €5.4 billion; it wrote the whole sum off within two years. It would pay another €1.65 billion to license Nokia's patents for 10 years, over €5.4 billion in all. Nokia's Lumia phones led Windows Phone sales, but its overall share was falling against rivals. Steve Ballmer framed the deal as part of turning Microsoft into a "devices and services" company. Lumia phones took Microsoft branding, sales kept falling, and in 2015 Microsoft wrote down US$7.8 billion and laid off 7,800 people, mostly in its phone business.

Carl Benedikt Frey and Michael A. Osborne scored 702 occupations; high risk meant potentially automatable over perhaps a decade or two, and their study did not estimate how many jobs would be lost.

Work began in 2010 to serve future graphics processors and high-performance computing; four stacks could feed a GPU 512 GB/s to 1 TB/s.

silk-road-2013.summary: In October 2013 the FBI shut Silk Road, a dark web drug market, and arrested its founder, Ulbricht. Launched in 2011 under his pseudonym "Dread Pirate Roberts", Silk Road was the first modern darknet market, run as a hidden service on Tor with every purchase paid in bitcoin to shield buyers and sellers. In 2015 Ulbricht received two life sentences without parole; President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.

sorek-desalination-2013.summary: IDE Technologies built Sorek, a seawater reverse osmosis plant south of Tel Aviv, under a build-operate-transfer contract; it began operating in October 2013 with a capacity of 624,000 cubic metres a day, then the largest of its kind. It was the first large plant to use 16-inch membrane elements mounted vertically, which cut piping and footprint, and it sold water to Israel at about 58 US cents per cubic metre. Sorek alone supplied about a fifth of Israel's household water, and with Ashkelon, Hadera and Palmachim Israel drew around 40 percent of its drinking water from the sea by 2015, ending shortages from a 2000s drought. A second plant, Sorek B, was tendered in 2020.

healthcare-gov-2013.summary: In October 2013 HealthCare.gov crashed on launch, enrolling six people on its first day. Its rescue created the US Digital Service. Some estimates said only 1% of interested people enrolled in its first week. Todd Park first blamed unexpected traffic of 250,000 simultaneous users against 50,000 to 60,000 expected, but officials later acknowledged software and systems-design problems; stress tests one day before launch showed it slowing at only 1,100 users. By the December 23 deadline for January coverage, problems had largely been fixed.

odisha-phailin-evacuation-2013.summary: Cyclone Phailin makes landfall near Gopalpur, Odisha, around 9 pm on 12 October 2013 with winds near 200 kilometres per hour, strongest to strike India since a 1999 cyclone on this coast killed over 10,000 people. This time about 850,000 people in Odisha and 150,000 in Andhra Pradesh are moved to cyclone shelters and inland sites over two days, using India Meteorological Department forecasts, Odisha State Disaster Management Authority's shelter network built after 1999, sirens and door-to-door warnings. Reported deaths within 72 hours number 38. Odisha's response marks a shift from relief to preparedness, and Phailin becomes a reference for mass evacuation in cyclone-prone regions.

vae-2013.summary: In December 2013 Kingma and Welling introduced the variational autoencoder, which generates by learning to compress. VAEs pair an encoder network, which maps each input such as an image to one probability distribution in compressed latent space, with a decoder mapping points in that space back to data. That probabilistic design makes them generative models, able to produce new samples resembling their training data.

cuba-el-paquete-semanal-2014.summary: By the mid-2010s most Cuban households received films, television series, music, software, phone apps, magazines and classified listings offline, through El Paquete Semanal, a weekly compilation of about a terabyte assembled by a few 'matrices' in Havana from satellite downloads and slow connections, then copied onto hard drives and USB sticks by thousands of distributors who delivered to homes for one or two dollars. With home internet nearly absent and state television limited, El Paquete carried Korean dramas, Miami talk shows, Cuban reggaeton and the Revolico classifieds site; it avoided pornography and open politics to limit state interference. Steffen Köhn's 2019 study documents its workflow and its tolerated semi-legal status.

Over two decades Department of Biotechnology, Bharat Biotech, PATH, US National Institutes of Health and CDC develop it into an oral vaccine. A trial in 4,532 infants at three Indian sites, published in 2014, shows 56 percent efficacy against severe rotavirus gastroenteritis in first year. India licenses Rotavac in 2014, Bharat Biotech prices it near one dollar a dose, Universal Immunization Programme adds it from 2016, and WHO prequalifies it in 2018, opening supply to Gavi countries.

seq2seq-2014.summary: In 2014 two papers showed one network could read a sentence into a vector and another write it out in a new language. Sutskever, Vinyals and Le wrote “Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks,” and Kyunghyun Cho's Montreal group wrote “Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation,” dated June 3, 2014. In seq2seq, one neural network, its encoder, compresses input such as a sentence into one vector of numbers, and a second, its decoder, expands that vector into output. Because that vector has fixed size, long inputs lost information, which attention mechanisms later addressed.

Microsoft spun off its Xiaoice business as a separate company on 13 July 2020; by 2022 the brand reached 660 million online users.

Its HiSeq X Ten claimed the first $1,000 genome at 30x coverage; that catchphrase dated from 2001 and the Human Genome Project's cost. Michael Schatz of Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory called its release a major milestone, while critics noted its $10 million upfront cost and that Illumina's estimate excluded data storage, though it included some overhead; clients were then paying $1,600 to $1,800. By 2018 companies briefly offered whole genomes for under $200.

mt-gox-2014.summary: In February 2014 Mt Gox, handling most of the world's bitcoin trades, collapsed saying 850,000 coins were missing. One leaked internal crisis document said it was insolvent after losing 744,408 bitcoins in a theft undetected for years; 200,000 were later found, and researchers showed its stated cause, transaction malleability, cannot explain that loss. It filed for bankruptcy protection in Tokyo on February 28 with liabilities of about 6.5 billion yen against assets of 3.84 billion yen. Its collapse and former CEO Mark Karpelès's conviction led Japan to write its first formal regulations for cryptocurrency exchanges.

mh370-inmarsat-analysis-2014.summary: Flight MH370, a Boeing 777 with 239 people from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, loses contact with air traffic control at 17:22 UTC on 7 March 2014 and turns back across Malay Peninsula before leaving military radar range. Inmarsat engineers find seven hourly log-on 'handshakes' from its satellite terminal and use burst timing offsets and Doppler-shifted frequency offsets to show it flew south for six more hours into Indian Ocean. This analysis, never before used for navigation, defines search zones for Australian-led seabed surveys that scan 120,000 square kilometres without finding wreckage. india-polio-free-2014.summary: WHO's South-East Asia Region was certified polio free on 27 March 2014, three years after India's last wild poliovirus case, a girl in Howrah, West Bengal, on 13 January 2011. India had recorded over half of world's cases as late as 2009. National Immunization Days delivered oral polio vaccine to about 170 million children under five in each round through 2.3 million vaccinators, with booth days, house to house sweeps, transit teams at stations and tracking of migrant families in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Monovalent and bivalent oral vaccines introduced from 2005 and 2010 raised efficacy against type 1 and 3. Surveillance of acute flaccid paralysis and environmental sewage sampling sustained certification.

Named after a synthetic intelligence in Microsoft's Halo games and voiced in the US by that character's actress Jen Taylor, it came to Windows 10 desktops in 2015 and to Xbox One. Microsoft shut down its mobile app worldwide on March 31, 2021, and its Windows app in 2023; Cortana is now deprecated and discontinued.

heartbleed-2014.summary: In April 2014 Heartbleed revealed a bug in OpenSSL that let anyone read servers' memory; two thirds of the web had trusted it. OpenSSL is widely used to encrypt web traffic; this bug, introduced in 2012, let anyone read more server memory than allowed through TLS's heartbeat extension, exposing private keys, session cookies and passwords. About 17% of trusted secure web servers, roughly half a million, were believed vulnerable at disclosure. It affected OpenSSL 1.0.1 through 1.0.1f and was registered as CVE-2014-0160.

kiribati-fiji-land-purchase-2014.summary: Kiribati's 33 atolls mostly lie under three metres above sea level. President Anote Tong's government paid about 9.3 million Australian dollars to Church of England for 2,200 hectares at Natoavatu on Fiji's Vanua Levu, completing payment in May 2014. Tong framed purchase as food security and a possible refuge under his 'migration with dignity' policy, while Fiji's prime minister Frank Bainimarama said I-Kiribati would be welcome. Among I-Kiribati, land in Fiji raised and complicated imaginings of migration. Land is hilly, partly forested and already home to descendants of Solomon Islanders; later government used it for farming rather than settlement.

right-to-be-forgotten-2014.summary: In May 2014 the EU's top court ruled that search engines process personal data and, in certain circumstances, must remove links shown in searches for a person's name; Google got a million requests. Costeja González had asked Google to drop links to 1998 newspaper notices about his resolved social security debts. Delisting may apply when information is inadequate, irrelevant, no longer relevant or excessive, balanced against public interest in access. In 2019 the Court limited this right to EU versions of search engines rather than every version worldwide.

nigeria-ebola-containment-2014.summary: On 20 July 2014 Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American already ill with Ebola, flew into Lagos, a city of over 20 million, and collapsed at the airport. Nigeria's health ministry and Lagos State turned an emergency operations centre built for polio eradication, with its GIS tools and trained field officers, into an Ebola incident command within days. Teams identified 894 contacts in Lagos and Port Harcourt and made about 18,500 home visits. Transmission ended at 19 confirmed and one probable case with eight deaths, and WHO declared Nigeria Ebola-free on 20 October 2014. Rapid isolation and contact tracing stopped an outbreak in a megacity while Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia were overwhelmed.

Participants claimed to defend ethics in games journalism, which critics widely dismissed as baseless. Gamergate became a template for later coordinated online harassment and is viewed as having fed the alt-right.

swachh-bharat-mission-2014.summary: On 2 October 2014, Gandhi's birthday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Swachh Bharat Mission with the goal of ending open defecation in rural India by 2019. Household toilet coverage stood at about 39 percent. With cash incentives of 12,000 rupees per latrine, village-level behaviour campaigns and a monitoring app, the programme recorded more than 100 million household toilets by October 2019 and declared all 600,000 villages open-defecation free; by November 2025 the count stood near 120 million. Independent surveys found usage lagging construction in some states. A 2024 study in Scientific Reports across 640 districts linked toilet construction above 30 percent of households to 5.3 fewer infant deaths per 1,000 births, roughly 60,000 to 70,000 infant deaths averted a year. Phase II, to 2026, funds solid and liquid waste management.

It came to rest in shadow beneath a cliff, and on 15 November its batteries ran down and it fell silent. Rosetta photographed it lying on its side on 2 September 2016, then ended its own mission by descending onto the comet on 30 September.

resnet-2015.summary: In 2015 Microsoft's ResNet showed how to train networks hundreds of layers deep, a trick now inside nearly every AI model. It won that year's ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge. Stacking too many layers had made networks train worse, a “degradation” problem; ResNet's layers instead learn residual functions, with skip connections that pass each layer's input forward alongside its output. That residual connection let networks hundreds of layers deep train stably, and it became a common motif in transformers such as BERT and GPT, AlphaGo Zero and AlphaFold.

nepal-earthquake-crisis-mapping-2015.summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes Nepal on 25 April 2015, killing about 9,000. deepdream-2015.summary: In July 2015 Google released DeepDream, which ran an image recogniser in reverse until dogs and eyes grew out of every photo. Created by Google engineer Alexander Mordvintsev from a network codenamed Inception built for the 2014 ImageNet challenge, it uses a convolutional neural network to find and enhance patterns in images, so that repeated passes produce dream-like, psychedelic pictures by algorithmic pareidolia. After Google open-sourced its code, web services and apps appeared letting people transform their own photos.

ethereum-2015.summary: In 2015 Ethereum went live, a blockchain that runs programs, so code could hold and move money by its own rules. Programmer Vitalik Buterin had described it in a late-2013 white paper as a blockchain that runs smart contracts, code that holds and moves assets by its own rules, so anyone can deploy decentralized applications. Its currency, ether, is second only to bitcoin in market capitalization.

ebola-ring-vaccine-trial-2015.summary: In 2015 a trial in Guinea vaccinated contacts of Ebola cases and found no Ebola cases from 10 days after vaccination in immediately vaccinated clusters. In ring vaccination, contacts and contacts of contacts of each confirmed case are vaccinated, either at once or after a 21-day delay. Final results, published in December 2016, reported rVSV-ZEBOV to be highly protective, and the vaccine was approved in the European Union and United States in 2019 as Ervebo.

neural-style-transfer-2015.summary: In August 2015 Gatys, Ecker and Bethge introduced neural style transfer, which uses a VGG-19 network pretrained for object recognition on ImageNet to redraw one image, such as a photograph, in another image's visual style, such as a painting's. CVPR accepted their paper in 2016, and in 2017 Google AI showed one network learning many styles at once.

gravitational-waves-detected-2015.summary: In September 2015 LIGO detected ripples in spacetime from two black holes merging, a century after Einstein predicted them. Gravitational waves are ripples in spacetime, predicted by Albert Einstein in 1916 from general relativity, that spread outward when masses accelerate; the signal matched two black holes merging about 1.4 billion light years away. Previously such waves had only been inferred from pulsar timing. LIGO and Virgo announced the discovery on 11 February 2016.

volkswagen-dieselgate-2015.summary: In September 2015 US regulators revealed Volkswagen had rigged 11 million diesel cars to cheat emissions tests. It alleged that Volkswagen and Audi cars with 2-litre TDI diesel engines sold in the US from 2009 to 2015 carried defeat-device software that switched emissions controls on only during testing, letting them emit up to 40 times legal nitrogen oxide limits in normal driving. EPA ordered 482,000 cars recalled, CEO Martin Winterkorn resigned, and by mid-2020 this scandal had cost VW $33.3 billion in fines, settlements and buybacks.

sustainable-development-goals-2015.summary: In September 2015 193 countries adopted 17 Sustainable Development Goals for 2030; every aid agency reorganised its reports around them. Their stated aim is “peace and prosperity for people and the planet,” from ending poverty and hunger to tackling climate change and preserving oceans and forests, with most targets due by 2030. The UN's 2025 report found only 35% of targets on track or making moderate progress and 18% in reverse.

alphago-fan-hui-2015.summary: In October 2015 AlphaGo beat the European Go champion five games to nothing, a decade before experts expected a machine to do it. Built by Google's DeepMind, it picks moves with Monte Carlo tree search guided by deep neural networks trained on human and self-play games. No computer Go program had beaten a professional on a full-sized board without handicap before. DeepMind held the result until 27 January 2016 to coincide with its Nature paper describing the algorithms, and in March 2016 AlphaGo beat 9-dan professional Lee Sedol 4 games to 1.

tesla-autopilot-2015.summary: In October 2015 Tesla switched on Autopilot by software update; cars steered themselves on motorways and drivers were told to keep hands on. Autopilot is a driver-assistance system that steers within its lane and adjusts speed to traffic, corresponding to Level 2 partial automation as defined by SAE International, with drivers still responsible. Early versions used sensor and computing hardware from Mobileye, a partnership Tesla dissolved in July 2016.

theranos-2015.summary: In October 2015 the Wall Street Journal's John Carreyrou reported Theranos ran most tests on ordinary machines; a $9 billion company was built on a claim. Theranos, a blood-testing startup valued by press at $9 billion (a Justice Department filing put its stock at over $4 billion at end 2014), claimed to run tests on a few drops of blood. Theranos called his allegations factually and scientifically erroneous, and Walgreens suspended plans to expand its blood-testing centers. Former employee Tyler Shultz was a key source. Theranos dissolved in September 2018, and founder Elizabeth Holmes was convicted of fraud in January 2022 and sentenced to over 11 years in prison.

Based on former employees' accounts, it alleged that Theranos was not using its own technology for most blood tests and that its test accuracy was in doubt. Theranos denied those allegations. Carreyrou's story began an unraveling of a $9 billion company that ended with Theranos dissolving in September 2018.

mariana-fundao-dam-collapse-2015.summary: On 5 November 2015 Fundão iron-ore tailings dam of Samarco, a joint venture of Vale and BHP Billiton, liquefied and collapsed near Mariana, Minas Gerais. About 40 million cubic metres of slurry buried Bento Rodrigues village, killed 19 people, and travelled 650 kilometres down Rio Doce to its Atlantic mouth in 17 days, cutting water supply to 250,000 people and smothering fish and riverbank forest. Ecologists called it Brazil's worst environmental disaster, and Vale's Brumadinho dam failed in like manner in January 2019, killing 270. Investigations blamed upstream-raised construction and drainage failures under rising deposition. A 2024 settlement proposal reached about 25 billion dollars, with cases also heard in English courts.

Krenak Indigenous communities along Rio Doce lost fishing and ceremonial use of their river. Reparations run through Renova Foundation, criticised for slow resettlement of Bento Rodrigues.

tensorflow-2015.summary: In November 2015 Google open-sourced TensorFlow; any programmer could train the networks Google used. Google Brain built it by refactoring DistBelief, its proprietary deep learning system begun in 2011, into a library for training and running neural networks for Google's research and production. TensorFlow became one of the most popular deep learning frameworks alongside PyTorch; version 2.0 followed in September 2019.

zika-brazil-microcephaly-2015.summary: Zika virus, carried by Aedes aegypti, spread through Northeast Brazil from early 2015. In October paediatric neurologists in Recife, among them Vanessa van der Linden, reported a cluster of newborns with microcephaly, and on 11 November 2015 Brazil's Ministry of Health declared a national public health emergency. On 17 November Brazilian laboratories detected Zika RNA in amniotic fluid of two affected pregnancies in Paraíba, and PAHO issued an alert. A Rio de Janeiro cohort led by Patrícia Brasil, published in New England Journal of Medicine, found abnormal outcomes in about 42 percent of infected pregnancies. WHO declared a global emergency in February 2016. Brazil recorded more than 2,000 confirmed congenital cases by 2017, concentrated among poor families in Northeast states.

zika-brazil-microcephaly-2015.detail: Lancet Infectious Diseases tracked how confidence in this causal link built through early 2016. Research by Fiocruz, Instituto Evandro Chagas and Brazilian universities identified an Asian lineage virus and its neurotropism; a mosquito that eradication had removed in 1958 was again endemic nationwide. This epidemic prompted debate on Brazil's abortion law and on long-term care for affected children.

international-solar-alliance-2015.summary: On 30 November 2015, opening day of COP21 in Paris, Narendra Modi and François Hollande launch International Solar Alliance, a platform for countries lying wholly or partly between tropics of Cancer and Capricorn to pool demand and finance for solar power. Its declaration speaks of mobilising over 1,000 billion dollars in solar investment by 2030. India hosts its secretariat at Gurugram and contributes land and seed funding; a framework agreement signed in 2016 makes it a treaty body in December 2017, later opened to all UN members, with over 100 signatories by 2024. Jha's 2023 study places it in India's climate diplomacy. Its programmes run from solar pumps to a proposed global grid interconnection.

chan-zuckerberg-initiative-2015.summary: In December 2015 the Zuckerbergs pledged 99 percent of their Facebook shares, then $45 billion, to a company rather than a charity. They committed 99% of their Facebook shares over their lifetimes to philanthropy including science and education. CZI is set up as a limited liability company rather than as a traditional foundation, an example of philanthrocapitalism. In September 2016 it pledged $3 billion over ten years toward curing, managing or preventing all disease by 2100, including $600 million for Biohub in San Francisco.

openai-founded-2015.summary: In December 2015 OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit with $1 billion pledged to make AI benefit everyone. Its other founders were Ilya Sutskever, Greg Brockman, Trevor Blackwell, Vicki Cheung, Andrej Karpathy, Durk Kingma, John Schulman, Pamela Vagata and Wojciech Zaremba. Musk, Altman, Brockman, Reid Hoffman, Jessica Livingston, Peter Thiel, Amazon Web Services and Infosys pledged $1 billion in capital. Its charter set its mission as ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. It created a for-profit subsidiary in 2019, and its ChatGPT release in November 2022 set off an AI boom.

paris-agreement-2015.summary: In 2015 nearly every country agreed to hold global warming well below 2 degrees, the first deal binding all. It was adopted by consensus by 196 parties at COP21's close and commits them to pursue efforts to limit warming to 1.5 °C. It entered into force on 4 November 2016 after enough parties, including the European Union, had ratified it.

Translation comes by synthesized speech; it also translates instant messages into more than 70 languages. Spoken translation covers English, French, German, Mandarin, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Japanese and Russian.

falcon-9-first-landing-2015.summary: In 2015 a Falcon 9 booster landed upright after an orbital launch, the first to do so; launch costs began to fall. Its first stage had carried 11 Orbcomm-OG2 satellites to orbit before landing at Landing Zone 1 near its launch site. It was the first successful return and vertical landing of an orbital rocket's first stage, capping SpaceX's five-year effort toward reusable rockets meant to cut launch costs.

aerofarms-newark-vertical-farm-2016.summary: In September 2016 AeroFarms begins production at 212 Rome Street, Newark, New Jersey, on the site of former steel supplier Grammer, Dempsey and Hudson, filling nearly 70,000 square feet with grow tables stacked 12 layers to 36 feet, roots misted in aeroponic cloth beds under LEDs. Associated Press reports an industry group calling it the world's largest commercial vertical farm, planned at 2 million pounds of greens a year with crops in about 16 days against 30 in the field. Benke and Tomkins's 2017 review sets such farms in the context of urbanization, land scarcity and electricity cost, their binding constraint. The sector raised billions from 2017 to 2022, then AeroFarms filed for bankruptcy in June 2023 as Fifth Season closed and AppHarvest liquidated; Palm Ventures bought AeroFarms in April 2026.

burkina-bt-cotton-reversal-2016.summary: Burkina Faso, Africa's largest cotton producer, introduced Monsanto's insect-resistant Bt cotton in 2008 and by 2014 it covered nearly three quarters of planted area, cutting pesticide spraying. Yet INERA tests had shown Bt fibres running shorter than conventional varieties, and ginners found lint quality falling below premium grades Burkinabe cotton had commanded. In 2015 and 2016 cotton companies, led by Sofitex, cut Bt planting to zero and sought compensation of about 48 billion CFA francs, settling with Monsanto in 2017. Burkina Faso had been held up as a showcase for GM crops among smallholders, and its reversal reshaped debate on biotechnology across Africa.

delhi-odd-even-2016.summary: From 1 to 15 January 2016 Delhi's government allows private cars on roads only on alternate days by last digit of their number plates, with exemptions for women drivers, two-wheelers and CNG vehicles, enforced by police and volunteers. Winter smog had pushed fine particulate levels far above limits. Economists Greenstone, Harish, Pande and Sudarshan compare 23 Delhi monitors against Faridabad, Gurgaon and Noida and estimate a 10 to 13 percent relative fall in particulates, about 18 percent during 8 am to 8 pm hours. A repeat in April 2016 shows little effect and later rounds in 2017 and 2019 are contested. Odd-even becomes a recurring emergency measure while studies point to crop burning and road dust as larger sources.

katanga-cobalt-amnesty-2016.summary: On 19 January 2016 Amnesty International and Afrewatch published 'This is what we die for', following cobalt from artisanal pits around Kolwezi in the Democratic Republic of the Congo through traders and a Chinese refiner into batteries sold by major electronics and car brands. Miners, including thousands of children, dug tunnels by hand without protective equipment and accidents were common. The Katanga Copperbelt supplies more than half of world cobalt, with 15 to 20 percent from artisanal diggers. Later measurements of blood and urine from Kolwezi residents found much higher cobalt levels and signs of DNA damage in children. The report pushed battery makers toward supply-chain audits and 'cobalt-free' chemistries.

great-barrier-reef-bleaching-2016.summary: In March and April 2016, sea temperatures up to 1.5 degrees above normal, driven by global warming and an El Nino, bleached 91 percent of 1,156 surveyed reefs along Great Barrier Reef. Aerial and underwater surveys led by Terry Hughes found northern third, previously least disturbed, lost around two-thirds of shallow corals within nine months, mostly rapidly growing branching and tabular species. Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority's final report recorded 29 percent coral loss reef-wide. A second bleaching in 2017 hit central section, so that 1,500 kilometres of reef bleached in consecutive years, with no time to recover. Hughes argued local water-quality and fishing controls offered little protection against heat.

ujjwala-lpg-2016.summary: Launched by Narendra Modi at Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, on 1 May 2016, Ujjwala pays deposit for a liquefied petroleum gas cylinder and regulator for women in below poverty line households, with stoves on loan. belo-monte-dam-2016.summary: On 5 May 2016 President Dilma Rousseff inaugurated Belo Monte near Altamira, Pará, weeks after its first 611-megawatt turbine began commercial operation on 20 April; full installed capacity of about 11,233 megawatts, reached in 2019, placed it among four largest hydroelectric plants worldwide. Its run-of-river design uses a canal to divert most of Xingu river around Volta Grande, a 100-kilometre bend home to Juruna and Arara communities, flooding roughly 440 to 500 square kilometres and reducing flow around Volta Grande, with output averaging well below capacity in dry seasons. Planned from 1975 as Kararaô and stopped by 1989 protests, the project was revived under Lula and built by consortium Norte Energia for about 40 billion reais. It remains Brazil's most contested energy project.

His Model S struck a tractor-trailer's underside in Williston, Florida; Tesla said neither Autopilot nor Brown noticed that trailer's white side against a brightly lit sky, so brakes were never applied. This crash prompted a federal NHTSA investigation of Tesla's technology.

compas-propublica-2016.summary: In 2016 ProPublica showed a sentencing algorithm wrongly flagged Black defendants as future criminals at nearly twice the rate of whites, 44.9 against 23.5 percent. Its analysis focused on classification errors, or how often the algorithm wrongly predicted whether a defendant would reoffend; Northpointe disputed its analysis, and a separate 2010 Florida State University study had found its scores predicted recidivism equally accurately regardless of race. That dispute over which fairness measure counts inspired a wave of empirical research on algorithmic risk tools.

panama-canal-expansion-2016.summary: On 26 June 2016 container ship Cosco Shipping Panama made first commercial transit of new Agua Clara and Cocolí locks, ending a nine-year, roughly 5.4 billion dollar project approved by referendum in 2006. Each new lock chamber, 427 metres long and 55 wide, uses rolling gates and three water-saving basins that recycle about 60 percent of water per lockage, a concern for a canal fed by Gatún Lake rainfall. Ships up to about 13,000 TEU, nearly three times prior Panamax capacity, and LNG carriers could now pass, redirecting Asia to US East Coast trade and prompting port dredging from Savannah to New York. Consortium Grupo Unidos por el Canal, led by Sacyr, finished two years late amid cost claims.

panama-canal-expansion-2016.detail: Canal operation depends on management of its watershed, and droughts in 2019 and 2023 forced draft and transit limits. Original 1914 locks measure 320 by 33.5 metres and still operate alongside new ones; a new Pacific access channel and deepened Gatún Lake raised draught to 15.2 metres. GUPC claimed more than 3 billion dollars in cost overruns, partly over concrete and seismic specifications, and arbitration ran for years. Revenue passed 3 billion dollars a year by 2019.

Players walk through their surroundings while GPS places Pokémon on a map, and their phone camera can show them as if standing in the street. It became one of 2016's most popular apps, passed 500 million downloads worldwide, had earned over $6 billion by 2020, and was credited with popularizing augmented reality and location-based games.

Founded in 2014 by Naveen Rao, Amir Khosrowshahi and Arjun Bansal, Nervana offered cloud software for building deep learning systems and was designing Nervana Engine, a chip stripped of graphics features and built only for deep learning. iran-national-information-network-2016.summary: On 28 August 2016 Iran's communications ministry inaugurates first phase of National Information Network (Shabake-ye Melli-ye Ettela'at), a project legislated in 2005 and built over a decade: domestic data centres, exchange points, a national DNS and pricing that makes traffic to Iranian hosts cheaper and faster than foreign traffic. Officials present it as sovereignty and resilience; rights groups read it as architecture for cutting Iran off while keeping banks, state media and local apps running. That reading is tested in November 2019, when authorities shut international connectivity for about a week during fuel protests while domestic services stay up, and again in 2022. Network also underpins state-backed messaging apps and search engines meant to displace Telegram and Google.

wavenet-2016.summary: In September 2016 DeepMind's WaveNet generated speech that sounded human. Earlier text-to-speech either stitched together recorded fragments or assembled sounds from mathematical models, both with unnatural cadence. WaveNet's convolutional network instead generates the raw waveform one sample at a time, 16,000 per second, after training on recorded English and Mandarin speech. Tests reportedly beat Google's best existing systems, and after a 1,000-fold speedup in October 2017 WaveNet began voicing Google Assistant.

pytorch-2016.summary: In 2016 Facebook built PyTorch, released publicly in January 2017, a deep learning library that read like Python; researchers switched to it and most AI papers use it. Developed at Facebook as successor to the Lua-based Torch library, PyTorch is an open-source Python library for building and training neural networks, with tensors as its basic data type. It became one of deep learning's most popular libraries alongside TensorFlow; ChatGPT, Tesla Autopilot and Hugging Face's Transformers are built on it, and it is now developed under the Linux Foundation.

samsung-galaxy-note-7-2016.summary: In September 2016 Samsung recalled its Galaxy Note 7 after batteries caught fire; airlines banned it and the recall cost $5 billion. A manufacturing defect in batteries had caused some phones to overheat and catch fire or explode. After replacement phones also caught fire, Samsung recalled Note 7 worldwide on 10 October and permanently ceased production a day later. Credit Suisse analysts estimated Samsung's loss at $17 billion in revenue; a refurbished Galaxy Note Fan Edition followed in July 2017.

americas-measles-elimination-2016.summary: On 27 September 2016 Pan American Health Organization's International Expert Committee declared Americas free of endemic measles transmission, after no endemic case since 2002 across 35 countries; it followed rubella elimination in 2015. The result rested on a 1990s strategy of catch-up, keep-up and follow-up campaigns with measles-mumps-rubella vaccine, coordinated by PAHO's Revolving Fund and national programmes from Mexico to Chile, and on laboratory surveillance networks. Status proved fragile: Venezuela lost it in 2018 and Brazil in 2019 as outbreaks spread from imported cases, the region regained verification in November 2024, and on 10 November 2025 Canada's twelve-month outbreak cost Americas regional status once more.

americas-measles-elimination-2016.detail: Mexico and United States faced large outbreaks in 2025. Catch-up campaigns vaccinated all children aged one to fourteen in a single month; follow-up campaigns every four years cleared accumulated susceptibles. Cuba had interrupted transmission by 1993 and English-speaking Caribbean by 1991. Loss of status in 2018 followed Venezuela's health system collapse, with cases exported to Brazil's Roraima; in 2025 Mexico's Chihuahua Mennonite communities and Canadian outbreaks drove loss again.

partnership-on-ai-2016.summary: In September 2016 Amazon, Facebook, Google, DeepMind, Microsoft and IBM formed the Partnership on AI to agree best practices. Its founding members were Amazon, Facebook, Google, DeepMind, Microsoft and IBM, with Eric Horvitz of Microsoft Research and Mustafa Suleyman of DeepMind as interim co-chairs. A nonprofit coalition formed to develop best practices for responsible AI, it grew to over 90 companies and nonprofits; Apple joined its board in January 2017, and its projects include the AI Incident Database.

south-australia-statewide-blackout-2016.summary: On 28 September 2016 tornadoes knocked down 23 transmission towers; voltage dips caused nine wind farms to cut output by 456 megawatts through protective settings, overloading Heywood interconnector from Victoria, which tripped, and state separated and collapsed within seconds. About 850,000 customers lost power; most were restored within hours, Eyre Peninsula took longer. AEMO's 2017 final report identified wind-farm ride-through settings as critical. Political blame on renewables prompted state to procure Hornsdale battery and backup gas turbines and led to new system-strength and ride-through rules.

Desktop still led in mature markets, at 58% in the United States and 55.6% in Britain, while India drew over 75% of its usage from mobile devices. StatCounter's CEO called it a wake-up call for businesses to make websites mobile friendly, noting that Google favored such sites in mobile search results.

It is set in a Wild West theme park where wealthy guests act out fantasies on android hosts programmed not to harm humans and reset each night, until added code lets the hosts become sentient. The series ran four seasons, ending in 2022.

addis-djibouti-railway-2016.summary: On 5 October 2016 Ethiopia's prime minister Hailemariam Desalegn and Djibouti's president Ismail Omar Guelleh opened a 752 km railway from Addis Ababa's Furi-Lebu station toward Djibouti's port, electrified at 25 kV and built from 2011 by China Railway Group and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation for about US$4 billion, mostly on Export-Import Bank of China loans. It replaces a metre-gauge line finished in 1917 under Menelik II's concession. Djibouti's section opened in January 2017 and commercial freight and passenger service began on 1 January 2018, with a Chinese consortium operating it for six years. Power shortages, debt renegotiation and livestock strikes marked early years.

Power supply failures, livestock collisions and debt renegotiation with China in 2018 marked its first years, and Ethio-Djibouti Railway company took over operation in 2024.

white-house-ai-report-2016.summary: In October 2016 the Obama White House published its first report on AI. Both followed five public workshops and a request for information that drew 161 responses. Its chapters addressed using AI for social good and government operations, adapting regulation for technologies such as automated vehicles, keeping AI fair, safe and governable, and building a skilled, diverse AI workforce.

zipline-rwanda-2016.summary: In October 2016 Rwanda began delivering blood by drone to rural hospitals, the first national drone delivery service. Zipline, a California robotics company, runs fixed-wing drones launched by catapult that fly themselves by GPS below 500 feet and drop blood packages by parachute without landing, with a range of 150 km. Plans called for up to 150 emergency deliveries a day to 21 transfusion facilities in Rwanda's western half, cutting waiting times from hours to minutes.

Many of those devices still used default usernames and passwords, which Mirai exploited. Its authors had first used Mirai to attack Minecraft servers, and after they posted its source code online, other criminals adapted it into new variants.

GNMT also learned an internal representation shared across languages, letting it translate directly between pairs it had never been trained on.

india-demonetisation-2016.summary: On 8 November 2016 India voided its 500 and 1,000 rupee notes overnight, and queues formed at banks for weeks. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said this move would curb India's shadow economy, push cashless payment and cut counterfeiting and terrorist financing; old notes were to be exchanged for new 500 and 2,000 rupee notes. People queued for hours, several deaths were linked to the rush, and industrial production and GDP growth fell. Digital payments rose sharply in November and December, but about 99.3 percent of the voided notes were deposited, leading analysts to judge that it failed to remove black money.

Its products cost US$10 to 200, carry two to four SIM slots for juggling networks, batteries lasting days, loudspeakers for music and camera exposure tuned for darker skin tones; a Carlcare service network and local assembly in Ethiopia backed them. Lu Miao's 2025 study treats Transsion as translation of Chinese mobile technology into African markets.

uruguay-wind-power-transition-2017.summary: Uruguay, which imported oil and suffered drought-driven power shortages between 2004 and 2008, adopted a cross-party energy policy in 2008 under physicist Ramón Méndez Galain as energy director. State utility UTE held auctions for long-term wind contracts, and private developers installed about 1,500 megawatts of turbines across its grasslands between 2013 and 2017, financed without subsidies by Uruguay's investment grade and stable contracts. In 2017 wind supplied roughly a third of electricity, hydro and biomass most of what remained, and renewables exceeded 97 percent of generation; Uruguay exported power to Argentina and Brazil. Remaining challenges include storage and electrification of transport.

Investment of about 7 billion dollars, near 15 percent of GDP, came through public-private contracts. Rural landowners receive lease payments and biomass plants burn cellulose and rice-husk residues. Uruguay's model is cited in debates on how small economies can decarbonise power without nuclear or large subsidies.

cameroon-internet-shutdown-2017.summary: On 17 January 2017 Cameroon's government ordered Camtel and mobile operators to suspend Internet service to Northwest and Southwest regions after lawyers' and teachers' strikes against marginalisation of English speakers. About five million people lost connectivity for 93 days until 20 April 2017. Start-ups in Buea's 'Silicon Mountain' moved staff to Douala and to roadside camps just inside Francophone regions to keep working; banks, hospitals and schools lost services. A #BringBackOurInternet campaign, lawsuits before Cameroon's Constitutional Council and UN criticism followed. A second shutdown ran from October 2017 to March 2018 as the crisis turned into armed conflict.

africa-cdc-2017.summary: On 31 January 2017 African Union heads of state launched Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention at AU headquarters in Addis Ababa, with Cameroonian virologist John Nkengasong as first director. Africa CDC began with an emergency operations centre, ten epidemiologists and five regional collaborating centres in Egypt, Nigeria, Gabon, Zambia and Kenya. It coordinated COVID-19 testing and vaccine procurement for member states and in 2022 became an autonomous agency.

turkey-wikipedia-block-2017.summary: On 29 April 2017 Turkey's Information and Communication Technologies Authority blocks every language edition of Wikipedia under Article 8/A of Internet Law 5651, after Wikimedia Foundation refuses to remove two English articles describing Turkish links to Syrian jihadist groups. Case becomes reference point for how courts weigh whole-platform blocking against single-page removal.

mombasa-nairobi-sgr-2017.summary: On 31 May 2017 President Uhuru Kenyatta rode the inaugural Madaraka Express over 472 kilometres of new standard gauge track from Mombasa to Nairobi. It parallels the metre-gauge Uganda Railway of 1901. Passenger trains run at up to 120 km/h and freight was expected to move in eight hours instead of a day by road. Wang and Wissenbach's interviews show Kenyan patronage politics shaping contracts and labour more than Chinese direction. Debt service, freight tariffs and a halt at Naivasha later made it a test case for Belt and Road lending.

puttaswamy-privacy-judgment-2017.summary: On 24 August 2017 nine judges of India's Supreme Court held unanimously in Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v Union of India that privacy is a fundamental right protected under Article 21 and other freedoms, overruling earlier decisions of 1954 and 1962. The case arose from challenges to India's Aadhaar biometric identity programme and the government's argument that no such right existed. Judges set a test of legality, legitimate aim and proportionality for state intrusions, including data collection. Its ruling framed a later Aadhaar judgment of 2018, decriminalisation of homosexuality, and Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, and is cited across common law courts on informational privacy.

kenya-election-annulled-2017.summary: On 1 September 2017 Kenya's Supreme Court, by four votes to two, nullified Uhuru Kenyatta's 8 August re-election and ordered a fresh vote within sixty days. Petitioners led by Raila Odinga argued that the electoral commission's KIEMS system had transmitted results without scanned forms 34A, that about a quarter of form images were unavailable when results were declared, and that server logs were withheld in defiance of a court order. Judges found illegalities and irregularities in transmission that affected the election's integrity, without ruling on who won. Odinga boycotted a repeat election on 26 October, which Kenyatta won with 98 percent on 39 percent turnout.

IEBC's results transmission system was supposed to send photographed forms from each polling station; many results arrived as text only, and IEBC declined a court-ordered audit of its servers. Chief Justice David Maraga's court became a reference point in later African election cases, including Malawi's 2020 annulment.

puerto-rico-hurricane-maria-grid-collaps.summary: On 20 September 2017 Hurricane Maria crossed Puerto Rico as a high-end Category 4 storm with 250 km/h winds, two weeks after Irma. Transmission towers carrying power from southern plants to San Juan fell, most of distribution network failed, and all 1.5 million customers of bankrupt utility PREPA lost electricity. Restoration took months: half of customers waited about three months and last ones until August 2018, more than ten months, making it the largest blackout in US history by customer-hours. Hospitals, water pumps and telecoms failed together; a Harvard-led household survey estimated excess deaths far above official count of 64, and government later revised the toll to 2,975.

puerto-rico-hurricane-maria-grid-collaps.detail: A Harvard-led household survey estimated 4,645 excess deaths; a George Washington University study later produced the 2,975 figure. Puerto Rico generates most power on south coast and consumes it in north, so 230-kilovolt lines across mountains are a chokepoint. PREPA had filed for bankruptcy in July 2017 with 9 billion dollars of debt. A 300 million dollar no-bid contract to two-person firm Whitefish Energy was cancelled amid scandal. Maria's blackout drove rooftop solar and battery adoption, PREPA's privatisation to LUMA Energy and debate over grid resilience in island territories. Act 17 of 2019 set a 100 percent renewable target for 2050.

cape-town-day-zero-2018.summary: After rainfall failures in 2015, 2016 and 2017 drained Western Cape dams below a quarter, Cape Town's city government announced in January 2018 that taps could run dry on 'Day Zero', then forecast for April, when residents would queue at 200 collection points. Restrictions of 50 litres a person a day, pressure management, tariff hikes and public dashboards cut consumption from about 1.2 billion to around 500 million litres a day, farmers released irrigation water, and winter rains in 2018 ended the threat. Climate attribution analysis found warming had made such a drought about three times more likely.

cape-town-day-zero-2018.detail: Mike Muller held that politics and poor planning, together with drought, created the crisis. Scientists tracked dam levels as Day Zero neared. Groundwater drilling, a desalination plant and water reuse schemes were commissioned but arrived after rains returned. A 2025 study by economists found household water use stayed well below pre-drought levels years later, suggesting a lasting behavioural shift.

palestinian-3g-west-bank-2018.summary: Jawwal and Wataniya Mobile launch 3G service across West Bank on 23 and 24 January 2018, years after neighbours moved to 4G. A 2016 World Bank study puts Palestinian operators' lost revenue from restrictions at up to 1.15 billion dollars over three years. A 2015 agreement, delayed again until late 2017, released 3G spectrum for West Bank only; Gaza stays on 2G until 2024 and Israeli operators move to 5G. Case is studied as spectrum as a tool of territorial control.

whatsapp-lynchings-india-2018.summary: Through mid 2018 forwarded videos and voice notes warning of child kidnappers circulate through WhatsApp groups in Indian towns and villages, and mobs beat strangers to death in Maharashtra, Assam, Tripura, Karnataka and elsewhere; more than a dozen are killed by July. India's IT ministry tells WhatsApp, with over 200 million Indian users, that a platform cannot be a mute spectator and demands traceability. On 20 July 2018 WhatsApp limits forwarding in India to five chats at a time and removes its one-tap forward button beside media, later extending a five-chat limit worldwide. Vasudeva and Barkdull's 2020 study examines how rumours spread through trusted groups. Traceability demands lead to India's 2021 intermediary rules.

uganda-social-media-tax-2018.summary: From 1 July 2018 Ugandans had to pay an excise duty of 200 shillings (about US$0.05) a day through mobile money before using WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter and some 60 'over the top' services, under an Excise Duty (Amendment) Act passed on 31 May 2018. President Yoweri Museveni had called for a tax on online 'gossip'. Regulator figures show Internet subscriptions fell from 18.5 million to 13.5 million within three months, and revenue came in far below targets as users turned to VPNs. Boxell and Steinert-Threlkeld found Twitter use dropped 13 percent while collective-action posts rose. In July 2021 government replaced it with a 12 percent duty on data.

coral-sea-cable-2018.summary: Solomon Islands had signed with Huawei Marine in 2016 to build a cable to Sydney. Vocus built Coral Sea Cable System, lit in December 2019. Capri's chapter treats it as early case of techno-nationalist decoupling of undersea infrastructure; Nidhal's 2024 report reviews PNG's regulatory environment and cable landscape after it.

egypt-hepatitis-c-screening-2018.summary: Egypt carried the world's heaviest hepatitis C burden, about 10 percent of adults, a legacy of mass antischistosomal injections with reused needles between 1950s and 1980s. After sofosbuvir reached market in 2013 at 84,000 dollars a course, Egypt's health ministry negotiates 900 dollars, then licenses local generics from Pharco and others at under 100 dollars, and treats patients through a national committee from 2014. From October 2018 to April 2019 its '100 Million Healthy Lives' campaign offers rapid antibody tests to every adult at 6,000 sites, screening 49.6 million people, confirming 2.2 million viraemic cases and treating more than 90 percent with sofosbuvir and daclatasvir. Prevalence falls below 0.5 percent, and in 2023 WHO places Egypt on its gold tier toward elimination.

Packages ran from 600 megabytes for about seven dollars to four gigabytes for thirty, against state salaries near thirty dollars a month, so uptake was slow at first but reached millions within two years; 4G followed in 2019. Mobile access fed independent media, small private businesses and, in 2021, nationwide protest coordination on 11 July, after which authorities throttled and blocked services.

cuba-mobile-internet-3g-2018.detail: Cuba had been one of its hemisphere's last offline national populations, circulating content through El Paquete Semanal hard drives. Subscriber figures come from ETECSA statements. Cuba's first fibre link, ALBA-1 from Venezuela, was lit in 2013; before then satellite capacity limited island to a trickle. Hourly Wi-Fi cards fell from two dollars to one between 2015 and 2017. Mobile internet enabled apps for remittances, ride hailing and private restaurants, and a 2019 Decree-Law 370 criminalised online content 'contrary to social interest'.

brumadinho-dam-collapse-2019.summary: At 12:28 on 25 January 2019 Dam I at Vale's Córrego do Feijão iron mine near Brumadinho, Minas Gerais, failed by static liquefaction, releasing about twelve million cubic metres of tailings that buried the mine's canteen and offices at lunchtime and swept through Vila Ferteco toward Paraopeba river. Some 270 people died, most of them Vale employees and contractors, three years after Samarco's Fundão dam collapsed at Mariana. An expert panel found the upstream-raised dam steep, saturated and brittle, with no warning before failure; German certifier TÜV SÜD had attested stability months earlier. Brazil banned upstream tailings dams in February 2019 and ordered decommissioning, Vale paid about 37.7 billion reais in a 2021 settlement, and executives faced homicide charges.

brumadinho-dam-collapse-2019.detail: Sentinel satellite radar and optical data recorded deformation at Dam I in months before failure. Death toll was reported as 259 confirmed plus 11 missing in 2020, later 270 confirmed. Dam I rose in ten upstream lifts from 1976 to 2013 to 86 metres and had been inactive since 2016. Brazil's mining agency had dozens of upstream dams registered in Minas Gerais. In 2024 Vale, BHP and Samarco agreed a 170 billion reais settlement for Mariana. Paraopeba river water supply for Belo Horizonte region was affected for years.

Students, doctors, journalists and traders lost access to exams, records, news and payments. In Anuradha Bhasin v Union of India (10 January 2020) Supreme Court held that internet access for speech and trade enjoys constitutional protection and shutdown orders must be published, reasoned, proportionate and reviewed, though it ordered no restoration. India has since led world in shutdown counts.

colombia-banana-tr4-2019.summary: On 8 August 2019 Colombia's agricultural institute ICA declared a national phytosanitary emergency after laboratories at Wageningen University confirmed Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense tropical race 4 in Cavendish plantations near Riohacha and Dibulla, La Guajira; Resolution 11912 of 9 August set quarantine measures. Soil-borne TR4 kills Cavendish, variety that replaced Gros Michel after race 1 wiped it out in the 1950s, has no cure and persists for decades; it had spread from Asia to Africa and Middle East and now reached a continent that exports most of world's bananas. About 185 to 200 hectares on six farms were destroyed and covered, and Ecuador, Costa Rica and Guatemala tightened border controls. Peru confirmed TR4 in 2021 and Venezuela in 2023.

Colombia exports about 100 million boxes of bananas a year, mostly from Urabá and Magdalena far from La Guajira, so growers installed disinfection stations, restricted farm access and tracked soil movement to keep those zones clean. black-summer-bushfires-australia-2019.summary: From September 2019 to March 2020, after record heat and drought, fires burned about 24 million hectares, including roughly 21 percent of Australia's temperate broadleaf forest, an unprecedented share. Thirty-three people died in fires and 3,000 homes were lost; smoke blanketed Sydney and Canberra and was linked to more than 400 deaths. Fire scientists attribute that scale to fuel dryness under climate change. A royal commission in 2020 recommended a national emergency declaration power and better aerial firefighting. Images of Mallacoota evacuees under red skies circulated worldwide; disaster intensified debate over Australia's coal exports and emissions targets.

Measles arrived from New Zealand in September 2019. By early January 2020 Samoa recorded 5,707 cases and 83 deaths in a population of 200,000. A state of emergency from 15 November closed schools; on 5 and 6 December a national shutdown sent vaccination teams door to door, lifting coverage above 90 percent.

abqaiq-khurais-drone-attack-2019.summary: Before dawn on 14 September 2019, 18 drones and 7 cruise missiles strike Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq stabilisation plant, largest crude processing site anywhere, and Khurais field, puncturing spheroid tanks and stabilisation towers. Output falls by 5.7 million barrels a day, about 5 percent of world supply, and Brent jumps 15 percent on Monday, largest one-day rise on record. Yemen's Houthi movement claims attack; Saudi Arabia and United States attribute weapons to Iran, and UN investigators later say they cannot confirm Yemeni origin. Aramco restores capacity by end of month using spare capacity and repairs. Episode shows cheap unmanned systems defeating Patriot batteries pointed elsewhere and prompts procurement of counter-drone systems across Gulf.

singapore-pofma-2019.summary: Parliament passes Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act on 8 May 2019 by 72 votes to 9 and it commences on 2 October 2019. First direction goes on 25 November 2019 to opposition figure Brad Bowyer over a Facebook post about state investment funds. Legal scholars in Singapore Academy of Law Journal weigh its scope against free speech; critics and tech firms object, while government cites foreign interference and viral falsehoods. Dozens of directions follow, many during COVID-19 and elections.

bolivia-lithium-aci-deal-cancelled-2019.summary: By Decree 4070 of 3 November 2019 Evo Morales's government repealed Decree 3738 of 7 December 2018, which had created a joint venture between state firm Yacimientos de Litio Bolivianos and ACI Systems of Baden-Württemberg to build a lithium hydroxide plant and battery-material production at Salar de Uyuni, with investment reported at 1.3 billion dollars and output targeted around 40,000 tonnes a year over seventy years. Potosí civic committee had struck for weeks demanding higher royalties and local benefit. Morales fled Bolivia days later amid a wider political crisis. Bolivia holds some of the world's largest lithium brine resources, but high magnesium content, altitude and rain complicate evaporation; later governments turned to Chinese and Russian direct-extraction partners, and output remained small into the 2020s.

bolivia-lithium-aci-deal-cancelled-2019.detail: Obaya in Extractive Industries and Society analyses Bolivia's state-led strategy and the ACI episode; Reuters and Deutsche Welle report cancellation. Investment reported as 1.3 billion dollars (Reuters) or 1.2 billion euros (DW); output targets range from more than 10,000 tonnes to 40,000 tonnes. Morales had declared lithium a strategic resource in 2008 and insisted on state control of brine extraction, with foreign partners limited to downstream chemistry. YLB's own 15,000-tonne carbonate plant at Llipi, started in 2018, reached output only in 2023 and produced far below nameplate. In 2023 to 2024 YLB signed with CATL-led CBC, Citic Guoan and Uranium One for direct lithium extraction pilots.

china-health-code-2020.summary: Hangzhou's government and Alipay introduced a health code on 9 February 2020, with WeChat following within days: residents filled in travel and symptom forms and received a green, yellow or red QR code, updated nightly from self-reports, location data and case databases, that guards checked before allowing entry to housing estates, transit, offices and shops. Yellow or red meant seven to fourteen days of quarantine. Within months codes ran in more than 300 cities for at least 900 million users and became mandatory for public life. Fan Liang's study examines how platform companies took on state functions and how opaque rules and data use raised concerns, which surfaced when Henan banks' depositors received red codes in 2022.

halicin-antibiotic-2020.summary: In February 2020 MIT researchers used deep learning to find halicin, an antibiotic that kills resistant bacteria. James Collins and Regina Barzilay led that team, with Jonathan Stokes as first author. Halicin killed drug-resistant bacteria including Acinetobacter baumannii in mice, and follow-up screening of more than 100 million molecules yielded further candidates.

singapore-tracetogether-2020.summary: GovTech Singapore launches TraceTogether on 20 March 2020, an app exchanging encrypted Bluetooth identifiers between nearby phones so health officials can reach close contacts of COVID-19 cases, with data held 25 days on devices and uploaded only after infection. Its BlueTrace protocol is published openly and copied by Australia's COVIDSafe. Wearable tokens for people without smartphones follow in June, and check-ins at malls and workplaces become compulsory, taking adoption past 90 percent of residents. Gerard Goggin's analysis places it among early state tracing apps and their trust problems. In January 2021 government admits police may access data under Criminal Procedure Code, then passes a law limiting such access to serious offences.

covidsafe-app-australia-2020.summary: Based on Singapore's TraceTogether Bluetooth code, COVIDSafe launched on 26 April 2020 with Prime Minister Scott Morrison likening downloads to sunscreen. A New South Wales evaluation found app identified 17 close contacts missed by conventional tracing between May and November 2020, none of whom tested positive, with sensitivity about 15 percent. New Zealand relied on a QR-based tracer instead. Government reported two cases found nationwide. App was decommissioned on 10 August 2022 after costing more than 21 million dollars, a cautionary case for digital public health.

nz-covid-elimination-2020.summary: On 23 March 2020, with 102 known cases, Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern's government announced a move to Alert Level 4, closing borders, schools and most businesses within 48 hours. Baker, Wilson and Blakely argued in BMJ that elimination rather than mitigation suited an island nation acting early. Case numbers peaked at 89 a day in early April and fell to zero; on 8 June 2020 last active case recovered and country lifted all domestic restrictions, as The Lancet reported. Managed isolation at border, rapid testing and contact tracing kept community transmission near zero for most of 2020 and 2021, with 25 deaths in 2020 against hundreds per million elsewhere.

Outbreaks in August 2020 and August 2021 (Delta) were contained with regional lockdowns. Elimination ended in late 2021 as Delta spread in Auckland and vaccination rose; borders reopened in 2022. Australia's states ran a similar suppression strategy. A 2024 Royal Commission reviewed costs, including stranded citizens and economic effects.

diffusion-ddpm-2020.summary: In June 2020 three Berkeley researchers made diffusion practical, the method behind today's image generators, which Jascha Sohl-Dickstein's group had introduced in 2015: turn noise back into pictures. Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel's denoising diffusion probabilistic models reverse a process that gradually turns images into noise, so they can generate new images from noise. On CIFAR-10, a standard set of small images, their samples reached an Inception score of 9.46 and an FID of 3.17, two measures of image quality where FID is better when lower.

beidou-3-completion-2020.summary: A Long March 3B from Xichang placed last BeiDou-3 geostationary satellite in orbit on 23 June 2020, completing a constellation of 24 medium-orbit, three inclined geosynchronous and three geostationary satellites that China declared operational in July. BeiDou grew from a two-satellite regional system in 2000 and Asia-Pacific coverage in 2012 to a global service offering positioning within metres, centimetre-level precise point positioning in Asia, short-message communication of up to 1,000 Chinese characters and search-and-rescue. Initial global service began on 27 December 2018, and 28 BeiDou-3 satellites had launched by end of 2019. BeiDou receivers now ship in most Chinese phones and vehicles and underpin Belt and Road infrastructure.

arecibo-telescope-collapse-2020.summary: Around 07:00 local time on 1 December 2020 remaining cables on tower 4 of Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico gave way and the 900-tonne platform suspended 137 metres above the spherical reflector crashed through it, shearing tower tops. An auxiliary cable had slipped from its socket on 10 August and a main cable snapped on 6 November; on 19 November National Science Foundation had decided on controlled decommissioning as unsafe to repair. Built in 1963, the telescope had measured Mercury's rotation, found the first binary pulsar, imaged near-Earth asteroids with its planetary radar and hosted Puerto Rican science education. Forensic studies found zinc creep in cable sockets, likely worsened by electroplasticity from decades of radar current, failed well below rated loads. NSF chose a STEM education centre over rebuilding.

arecibo-telescope-collapse-2020.detail: National Academies' 2024 report reviews failure mechanism and lessons; Clery in Science reported collapse and its aftermath. Collapse time given as about 7:00 AM by NSF and 7:54 AM by Thornton Tomasetti forensic report, which differ on local versus Eastern clocks. Arecibo's radar had tracked Hurricane-season storms and asteroids such as Bennu, and its 1974 message to M13 cluster became emblematic of SETI. Hurricane Maria in 2017 and earthquakes in January 2020 had damaged the site before cable failures. Investigators found socket failure modes unknown to engineering codes; UCF now operates a 12-metre antenna and education centre there.

neom-the-line-announced-2021.summary: On 10 January 2021 Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman unveils The Line in a televised address: a 170 kilometre linear city in NEOM, northwest Saudi Arabia, with no cars, streets or carbon emissions, all daily needs within a five-minute walk and end-to-end transit in twenty minutes. A July 2022 design shows two mirrored walls 500 metres high and 200 metres apart housing 9 million people on 34 square kilometres. Earthworks begin in late 2021 and cost estimates reach into trillions of dollars. In April 2024 Bloomberg reports first phase cut to 2.4 kilometres for under 300,000 residents by 2030, which officials deny before a 2025 strategic review pauses most work. Architects and planners debate it as revival of linear-city ideas and as spectacle for investment.

manaus-oxygen-collapse-2021.summary: On 14 January 2021 hospitals in Manaus, capital of Amazonas, exhausted medical oxygen as COVID-19 admissions far exceeded supplier White Martins's capacity; patients suffocated in wards, families bought cylinders on black markets, and Brazil's air force flew oxygen in while Venezuela sent trucks. A blood-donor study had estimated 76 percent of city residents infected by October 2020, leading some to argue herd immunity had been reached. Genomic surveillance showed a new lineage, P.1 or Gamma, with mutations N501Y, E484K and K417T, emerging in Manaus in November 2020, more transmissible and able to evade antibodies from prior infection. Gamma spread across Brazil and abroad, and a Senate inquiry faulted federal government warnings. Amazonas recorded more than 13,000 deaths.

manaus-oxygen-collapse-2021.detail: Manaus's seroprevalence estimate was later questioned for overestimating attack rate. Its first wave in April and May 2020 had filled mass graves at Parque Tarumã cemetery. In January 2021 daily oxygen demand rose to about 70,000 cubic metres against supply near 28,000. Patients were flown to other states, and Supreme Court ordered federal government to present a plan. Gamma accounted for most Brazilian cases by March 2021 before Delta displaced it.
