israel-mass-vaccination-data-2021.summary: Israel starts vaccinating on 20 December 2020 and, under a January 2021 agreement with Pfizer to share anonymised outcome data, reaches half its population with a first dose within seven weeks. Clalit Health Services, a fund covering 4.7 million members with decades of unified records, matches 596,618 vaccinated people to controls and reports in February 2021 that two doses cut symptomatic infection by 94 percent and severe disease by 92 percent, close to trial results. It is first population-scale evidence on an mRNA vaccine and guides rollout decisions across Europe and North America. Israel's integrated health IT, built from 1990s, and its early booster programme in July 2021 keep it a reference dataset through later variants.

ever-given-suez-blockage-2021.summary: On 23 March 2021 container ship Ever Given, 400 metres long and carrying 18,300 boxes, runs aground diagonally in southern Suez Canal during a sandstorm with winds near 40 knots. Suez Canal Authority dredgers, 14 tugs and a spring tide refloat it on 29 March; by then 422 ships queue at both ends and some carriers divert round Cape of Good Hope. Canal carries about 12 percent of global trade, and delays ripple through container schedules for months. Egypt impounds ship until a July settlement reported near 540 million dollars. Grounding exposes how ultra-large vessels built for economies of scale outgrew a waterway widened in 2015, and authority announces further widening of southern reach.

sri-lanka-fertilizer-ban-2021.summary: In April 2021 President Gotabaya Rajapaksa banned imports of synthetic fertiliser and agrochemicals, ordering an immediate switch to organic farming for all two million farmers, partly to save foreign exchange. Organic substitutes were unavailable at scale. Paddy output in 2021-22 maha season fell by roughly a fifth to a third, tea exports dropped, and rice imports and food inflation followed. Government reversed ban in November 2021 and paid compensation, but losses fed into 2022 economic collapse and protests that forced Rajapaksa out. Case became a reference point on agronomic limits of abrupt organic transitions and on nutrient budgeting for small farms.

wolbachia-dengue-trial-yogyakarta-2021.summary: Universitas Gadjah Mada and World Mosquito Program publish results of AWED, a cluster-randomised trial across 24 areas of Yogyakarta, in New England Journal of Medicine on 10 June 2021. Teams released Aedes aegypti eggs carrying wMel Wolbachia, a bacterium that blocks dengue virus replication, in 12 clusters between March and December 2017; it spread through local mosquito populations and persisted. Among 8,144 febrile participants screened at clinics, virologically confirmed dengue fell 77.1 percent and dengue hospitalisation 86.2 percent in treated areas compared with controls. Funded by Tahija Foundation, with Wellcome and Gates support, trial results led Indonesia's health ministry to extend releases to five more cities in 2023.

Afrigen's scientists built a lab-scale version of Moderna's mRNA-1273 from published sequence and formulation data by February 2022, then developed their own candidate, AfriVac 2121. Fifteen partners from Argentina to Vietnam have since joined, with first technology transfer to Biovac completed in September 2024. cuba-abdala-soberana-covid-vaccines-2021.summary: On 9 July 2021 regulator CECMED granted emergency authorisation to Abdala, a receptor-binding-domain subunit vaccine produced in yeast by Centro de Ingeniería Genética y Biotecnología, after a phase 3 trial in Havana and Santiago reported 92.3 percent efficacy against symptomatic disease. Instituto Finlay's Soberana 02, an RBD conjugated to tetanus toxoid, followed in August with a Soberana Plus booster; a three-dose scheme showed 92.4 percent efficacy in trial. Cuba vaccinated children from age two and by early 2022 about 90 percent of its population with domestic products, without mRNA or imported doses, and exported to Venezuela, Vietnam, Iran, Nicaragua and Mexico. Low per-dose cost and no need for deep freezing suited its clinics, though WHO prequalification was not obtained.

pegasus-project-spyware-2021.summary: On 18 July 2021 a consortium of 17 news organisations coordinated by Forbidden Stories, with Amnesty International's Security Lab, publishes Pegasus Project: a leaked list of 50,000 phone numbers selected by government clients of Israeli firm NSO Group, and forensic proof of Pegasus infections on phones of journalists, activists, lawyers and a murdered Saudi journalist's fiancée. Amnesty's methodology report, peer-reviewed by Citizen Lab, documents zero-click iMessage exploits defeating fully patched iPhones and releases an open-source Mobile Verification Toolkit. Clients identified include Saudi Arabia, UAE, Morocco, Bahrain, Mexico, India and Hungary. US Commerce Department blacklists NSO in November 2021, Apple sues, and Israel tightens export licences, while spyware market shifts to rivals such as Predator.

kazakhstan-bitcoin-mining-surge-2021.summary: After China bans cryptocurrency mining in May and June 2021, operators truck containers of ASIC machines across border to Kazakhstan, drawn by coal power at a few cents a kilowatt-hour and a 2020 law recognising mining. Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance estimates Kazakhstan's share of global bitcoin hashrate at 18.1 percent in August 2021, second after United States, up from 8 percent in April. Demand rises about 8 percent in a year, grid operator KEGOC reports shortfalls above 1,000 megawatts, and rolling blackouts hit southern cities from October. Government imports Russian power, caps new mining connections, taxes electricity for miners and raids unregistered farms; a week-long internet shutdown during January 2022 unrest cuts hashrate again, and share falls to 13 percent by early 2022.

sanatech-gaba-tomato-2021.summary: In September 2021 Tokyo start-up Sanatech Seed, working with Tsukuba University, begins commercial sales of Sicilian Rouge High GABA tomatoes, edited with CRISPR-Cas9 to truncate the autoinhibitory domain of glutamate decarboxylase so fruit holds about five times normal gamma-aminobutyric acid, marketed for blood pressure. It is the first CRISPR-edited food sold to the public. Japan's Ministry of Health accepted notification in December 2020 under rules treating edits without foreign DNA as conventional breeding, so no safety review or GM label applied, and seedlings went to home gardeners in May 2021. Satoko Nonaka's team had reported edited lines with 7 to 15 times GABA in 2017. By 2025 Japanese consumer uptake remained slow.

rtss-malaria-vaccine-who-2021.summary: After 30 years of development by GlaxoSmithKline with PATH, and a phase 3 trial in 15,459 children at 11 African sites showing 36 percent fewer clinical malaria cases over four years with a booster, RTS,S was piloted from 2019 in Ghana, Kenya and Malawi. On 6 October 2021 WHO recommended it for children in regions of moderate to high transmission, a first for any vaccine against a parasite; Director-General Tedros called it "a historic moment". Pilots in 900,000 children showed a 13 percent fall in all-cause mortality. In October 2023 WHO added R21/Matrix-M from Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, whose phase 3 trial in 4,800 children gave 75 percent efficacy at seasonal sites. By February 2026, 25 African countries were vaccinating, aiming at over 10 million children a year, where more than 260,000 under-fives die of malaria annually.

huduma-namba-court-ruling-2021.summary: Kenya amended its registration law in 2018 to create NIIMS, a central biometric database issuing each resident a Huduma Namba, and ran a mass enrolment drive in 2019. Courts had earlier halted a full rollout on data protection grounds. On 14 October 2021 Justice Jairus Ngaah ruled card rollout unlawful because government had not conducted a data protection impact assessment under Kenya's 2019 Data Protection Act, which he held applied to data already gathered.

South Africa briefed WHO on 24 November and WHO named B.1.1.529 Omicron, a variant of concern, on 26 November. Within three weeks it was in 87 countries. Rapid, open reporting earned travel bans on southern Africa within hours, which scientists and governments condemned as punishment for surveillance.

hunga-tonga-eruption-cable-2022.summary: On 15 January 2022 submarine volcano Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai erupted in largest explosion recorded by modern instruments, sending a plume 57 kilometres high and a tsunami across Pacific. Eruption triggered rapid seafloor density currents that cut Tonga's international cable to Fiji about 80 kilometres away and its domestic cable, which were buried under volcanic debris. Tonga, with 105,000 people, lost nearly all internet and overseas phone service, relying on a few satellite terminals. Repair ship Reliance restored international link on 22 February; domestic cable to Ha'apai and Vava'u took about 18 months. Event exposed dependence of Pacific states on single cables.

indonesia-nusantara-capital-law-2022.summary: Indonesia's parliament passes State Capital Law on 18 January 2022, signed as Law 3/2022 on 15 February, creating Nusantara Capital Authority to build a government city on 256,000 hectares near Balikpapan in East Kalimantan. Construction began in 2022, a first Independence Day ceremony was held there in August 2024, and financing and population targets remain contested.

chain-of-thought-2022.summary: In January 2022 Google researchers found that asking a language model to think step by step made it far better at reasoning. Jason Wei's team called it chain-of-thought prompting: show the model worked examples of step-by-step reasoning and it reasons through a problem before answering. Eight such examples let a 540-billion-parameter model set record accuracy on GSM8K math word problems, beating a fine-tuned GPT-3 with a verifier.

uzbekistan-cotton-forced-labour-ends-202.summary: On 1 March 2022 International Labour Organization reports that 2021 cotton harvest in Uzbekistan, which mobilises about two million pickers, was free of systemic child and forced labour, based on 11,000 interviews under its third-party monitoring with World Bank. Cotton Campaign, a coalition of 331 brands and rights groups that had boycotted Uzbek cotton since 2011, ends its call for boycott on 10 March 2022 in Tashkent. Change follows reforms under President Mirziyoyev from 2017: abolition of state production quotas in March 2020, criminalisation of forced labour, higher picker wages and transfer of farms to private 'cluster' processors. Monitors still record local coercion and restrictions on independent observers, and wages remain low.

turkey-earthquake-building-collapse-2023.summary: On 6 February 2023 magnitude 7.8 and 7.5 earthquakes rupture East Anatolian Fault nine hours apart, killing more than 53,000 people in eleven Turkish provinces and about 6,000 in northern Syria. Over 35,000 buildings collapse or need immediate demolition, many of them reinforced-concrete apartment blocks built after a 1998 seismic code that should have withstood shaking. Investigators find soft storeys, poor concrete, missing stirrups and 'construction amnesties' of 2018 that legalised millions of non-compliant structures for a fee. Low-rise older masonry often fares better than newer towers. Disaster drives arrests of contractors, a national rebuilding programme of 650,000 homes and renewed scrutiny of code enforcement in Istanbul, which faces a comparable fault.

derna-dam-collapse-2023.summary: In early hours of 11 September 2023, after Storm Daniel dropped around 350 mm of rain on Wadi Derna's catchment in a day, Bu Mansour dam (75 m) upstream of Derna overtopped and breached, and its surge destroyed Al-Bilad dam below it. A flood wave several storeys high swept central Derna into the sea. Libya's divided authorities confirmed over 4,000 deaths with about 8,000 missing; estimates range above 11,000. Both earthfill dams, built by a Yugoslav firm in 1970s, had known damage and no maintenance for years amid civil conflict. Analyses find the spillway far too small for the flood and warnings that never reached floodplain residents.

derna-dam-collapse-2023.detail: Flood volume is estimated at 39 million cubic metres against 22 million of upstream storage, a 30 to 50 year return period. Bu Mansour breached at about 2:40 a.m. Audits by Libya's state auditor in 2021 had noted that maintenance contracts awarded in 2007 and 2012 to a Turkish firm were never completed. Residents reported evacuation orders aimed at coastal areas while valley neighbourhoods received curfews that kept people indoors as water came.

pakistan-rooftop-solar-2024.summary: In 2024 Pakistan imported about 17 gigawatts of Chinese solar modules, double 2023 and close to a third of national generating capacity, without a national programme or auctions. Households, farms and factories installed panels on roofs and in yards, most of them off-grid or behind meter. Net-metered capacity rose from under 1 gigawatt in 2023 to over 5 gigawatts by 2025. Grid demand fell, pushing fixed costs onto remaining consumers, and in 2026 regulator NEPRA replaced net metering with lower net billing for new users.

kenya-gen-z-protests-2024.detail: Human Rights Watch found at least 30 killed on 25 June alone. Anniversary protests on 25 June 2025 brought further deaths. Scholars read the movement as a shift from ethnic to generational mobilisation enabled by social media. Organisers used an AI chatbot trained on bill text, Google Docs of MPs' votes and X Spaces drawing hundreds of thousands of listeners. Protests spread to Mombasa, Kisumu, Eldoret and Nakuru. Ruto dismissed most of his cabinet in July 2024 and later brought opposition figures into government.

mpox-clade-ib-pheic-2024.summary: From September 2023 health workers in Kamituga, a gold-mining town in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, saw mpox spreading among adults through sexual contact, unlike clade I's usual zoonotic pattern in children. Sequencing by Congolese and international teams in 2024 found a distinct lineage, named clade Ib, with APOBEC3-type mutations marking sustained human-to-human transmission. By August 2024 DRC had reported over 15,600 suspected cases and 537 deaths in a year, and clade Ib cases appeared in Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda and Kenya. Africa CDC declared a continental emergency on 13 August and WHO a public health emergency of international concern on 14 August 2024.

mpox-clade-ib-pheic-2024.detail: Emmanuel Hasivirwe Vakaniaki's team counted 241 suspected cases in Kamituga to February 2024 and proposed the clade Ib designation. Over 100 confirmed clade Ib cases appeared in four neighbouring countries in the month before WHO's declaration. Kamituga's economy draws miners, traders and sex workers, which shaped early spread. Vaccines reached DRC only in September 2024 through donations of MVA-BN from European Union and United States. Africa CDC and WHO ended their emergency declarations in September 2025 as cases declined.

Attack is first mass weaponisation of a consumer communications supply chain and prompts debate over humanitarian law and trust in imported electronics.

mexico-gm-maize-decree-usmca-2024.summary: On 20 December 2024 a dispute panel under United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement found that Mexico's February 2023 decree banning GM maize in tortillas and dough, and its plan to phase out GM feed and industrial maize, lacked risk-assessment basis under USMCA's sanitary chapter; Mexico, the largest buyer of US corn at about 17 million tonnes a year, said it disagreed but would comply, repealing those measures by decree on 5 February 2025. Weeks later Congress approved a constitutional amendment, in force in March 2025, declaring maize a national heritage and barring cultivation of GM maize while leaving imports untouched. The case linked Oaxaca's 2001 transgene controversy, Mexico's status as centre of maize origin and a trade system in which Mexico mills imported yellow corn for feed and native white corn for food.

xai-memphis-pollution-2025.detail: Oct 30, 2026: Judge Debra M. Brown of US District Court for Northern Mississippi denied xAI's motion to dismiss NAACP v. xAI Corp., No. 3:26-cv-00074. That Clean Air Act citizen suit, filed in April 2026 against xAI Corp. and its property subsidiary MZX Tech LLC, concerns 27 flatbed-trailer gas turbines at an unpermitted Southaven, Mississippi plant powering xAI's Memphis data centre, per Bloomberg Law's Benjamin Hernandez. Brown held those turbines are stationary sources needing permits, that NAACP may sue, and, in words TechCrunch's Anthony Ha quoted, that 'Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government's executive power'. Mississippi Today's Katherine Lin reported Brown found that a 2025 Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality letter treating such turbines as mobile sources did not alter her determination, and that she had two weeks earlier denied a US Department of Justice motion to dismiss; that department had intervened calling Grok vital for national security. Abre' Conner, NAACP director of environmental and climate justice: 'Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits.' Earthjustice and Southern Environmental Law Center represent NAACP; Vinson & Elkins, Boyden Gray and Butler Snow represent xAI and MZX Tech. No ruling yet on NAACP's request to halt those turbines pending permits.

lenacapavir-africa-rollout-2026.summary: PURPOSE 1, a trial published in the New England Journal of Medicine in July 2024, recorded zero HIV infections among 2,134 young women in South Africa and Uganda given lenacapavir injections every six months. The FDA approved it for prevention in June 2025. Under a Global Fund and PEPFAR arrangement with Gilead, which forgoes profit until generics arrive, first shipments reached Eswatini and Zambia in November 2025 and dosing began in December. About 20,000 people had started by end of May 2026, 49,000 by June, and around 100,000 by mid-August across nine countries including Kenya, Nigeria, Zimbabwe and South Africa; some 191,620 doses had been shipped by July. In Eswatini 10,000 doses sat undistributed. The goal is 3 million people by end-2028, with licensed generics at about 40 dollars a year expected from 2027.
